parsed.system_name: the library management and reporting system

requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library system or branch at the current or a historical date, including total items, new acquisitions, checked-in items, checked-out items, holds, adult fiction, and board books; checked-out items must count toward the total, and category groupings must be configurable by library system, such as fiction/non-fiction or format.

requirements.name: Acquisition Volume Trends
requirements.description: The system must use item acquisition dates to report material added during selectable periods, including the preceding 30, 60, or 90 days.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Overview
requirements.description: The system must provide authorized branch managers with an all-branch capacity view, allow drilldown to an individual branch, show capacity trends such as growth or shrinkage, and support comparison for up to 286 branches.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Navigation
requirements.description: The capacity view must allow users to filter and sort branches by region, library type, and current load.

requirements.name: Capacity Data Export
requirements.description: The system must allow users to export capacity-view data in CSV format.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Analysis
requirements.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space, with views by branch and for the library system, selectable date ranges such as Q1 or Q2, collection percentages based on item counts, circulation percentages based on checkouts, and shelf-space estimates based on item dimensions or item count when dimensions are unavailable.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Comparisons
requirements.description: The system must show shelf-space analysis for branches side by side, including genre-and-format percentages for circulations, collection holdings, and shelf space, so users can identify differences and outliers.

requirements.name: Batch Item Transfers
requirements.description: Authorized staff must be able to transfer selected batches of items between branches and other destinations, including mobile libraries, outreach programs, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, by changing item locations or generating pull lists; the operation must process approximately 9.6 million items without excessive database locking.

requirements.name: Transfer Candidate Queries
requirements.description: Staff must be able to query for candidate items for transfer using criteria such as genre, collection area, and circulation inactivity, including items that have not circulated for six months.

requirements.name: Saved Transfer Queries
requirements.description: Staff must be able to save transfer-candidate queries for repeated use, including monthly reuse, and make saved queries available for reuse or sharing.

requirements.name: Transfer Item Selection
requirements.description: Staff must be able to manually select individual titles or items from transfer-query results before executing a transfer, such as selecting 25 items from 100 candidates.

requirements.name: Transfer Location Updates
requirements.description: The system must update the location field and associated item records for selected items moved to a new location.

requirements.name: Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer.

requirements.name: Transfer Reversion
requirements.description: The system must return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or configured event, including a status change to sold or returned or checkout at the destination.

requirements.name: Transfer Audit History
requirements.description: The system must record transfer history for each item, including enough history to determine patterns such as five transfers within one year.

requirements.name: Transfer Confirmation Preview
requirements.description: Before execution, the system must show a transfer preview containing the item count and source and destination locations and require staff confirmation.

requirements.name: Transfer Undo
requirements.description: Staff must be able to undo an erroneous transfer after it has been initiated or completed.

requirements.name: Transfer Role Permissions
requirements.description: The system must restrict transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.

requirements.name: Transit Label Generation
requirements.description: The system must generate printable barcode transit labels for transferred items.

requirements.name: Transfer Delay Alerts
requirements.description: The system must notify designated staff when a transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Reports
requirements.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.

requirements.name: Overdue Transit Report
requirements.description: The system must provide one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.

requirements.name: Purge Candidate Identification
requirements.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.

requirements.name: Batch Status Conversion
requirements.description: The system must provide a report or workflow for converting many selected items from one status to another in one batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.

requirements.name: Last Copy Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report items that are the only copy within a selected branch, library system, consortium, bibliographic work, or collection grouping, including deleted last copies where applicable, so catalogers can update WorldCat and avoid inappropriate deletion.

requirements.name: Orphan Record Deletion
requirements.description: The system must provide a quick method to delete volume entries with their associated copy entries and records with no attached items.

requirements.name: Protected Purge Reports
requirements.description: Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.

requirements.name: Confirmed Purge Deletion
requirements.description: The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.

requirements.name: Purge Audit Trail
requirements.description: The system must record who purged each record and when.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Logging
requirements.description: The system must record completed and denied deletion attempts, including record type, record ID, timestamp, user, user branch, library system, and, where required, deletion reason; deletion data must support counts and queries by branch, system, date range, user, record type, and highest-volume users.

requirements.name: Patron Report Filtering
requirements.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.

requirements.name: Configurable Age Ranges
requirements.description: Users must be able to configure age ranges separately for each patron report, including ranges such as 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 or 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.

requirements.name: Null Demographic Inclusion
requirements.description: Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.

requirements.name: Inactive Report Scope
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must list or group results by configurable organizational scopes, including library system, home branch, and county, so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Outreach
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must include each patron's current mailing address and support CSV export for upload to an outreach system.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Exceptions
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.

requirements.name: Scalable Inactive Reporting
requirements.description: For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.

requirements.name: Open-Hours Performance
requirements.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.

requirements.name: Server Platform Support
requirements.description: The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.

requirements.name: Client And Browser Access
requirements.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
requirements.description: The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.

requirements.name: Standards Compliant HTML
requirements.description: Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.

requirements.name: Environment Separation
requirements.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.

requirements.name: Configuration Migration
requirements.description: The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.

requirements.name: Role Based Access Control
requirements.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups; changing a role assignment must change permissions. Supported levels include Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role.

requirements.name: OPAC Preservation
requirements.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.

requirements.name: Process Documentation
requirements.description: The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

requirements.name: Online System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions and is accessible within the system and to screen readers.

requirements.name: Error Feedback
requirements.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.

requirements.name: Staff Authentication
requirements.description: The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.

requirements.name: Report Template Controls
requirements.description: Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.

requirements.name: Report Permission Administration
requirements.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.

requirements.name: Multi Record Query Designer
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, Boolean operators, and administrator control over tables, fields, and tool access.

requirements.name: Executive Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.

requirements.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
requirements.description: The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.

requirements.name: Periodic Management Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide periodic reports for records with holds, items not checked out for a configurable period, item-level holds, invalid item types, in-transit items with holds, overdue transit, last copies, long call numbers, missing items, bibliographic records without items, and patrons with invalid home branches.

requirements.name: Query Criteria Display
requirements.description: Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.

requirements.name: Report Queue Monitoring
requirements.description: Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.

requirements.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
requirements.description: The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Control
requirements.description: The system must track uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books before catalog records exist, support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify usage, and include their transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

requirements.name: Collection And Capacity Analysis
requirements.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections, material use, branch capacity, patron demographics, staff workflow, financial transactions, and cross-branch performance for planning, evaluation, and oversight.

requirements.name: Consortium Statistical Reports
requirements.description: The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.

requirements.name: Data Quality Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.

requirements.name: Vendor Data Integration
requirements.description: Management processes must exchange standard-format data with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, and must continue to function when vendor data is unavailable at a branch.

requirements.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
requirements.description: Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.

requirements.name: OPAC Data Querying
requirements.description: Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.

requirements.name: Report Types
requirements.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.

requirements.name: Scheduled Canned Reports
requirements.description: Users must be able to run product-delivered canned reports using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data, select multiple canned reports, and combine their output in one document.

requirements.name: On Demand Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities.

requirements.name: Report Scheduling
requirements.description: Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.

requirements.name: Report Export Formats
requirements.description: Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system must deliver reports by email, allow users to enter recipients, and provide an address book for regularly used addresses.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Output
requirements.description: Reports must support comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage differences, and the corresponding month of the previous year.

requirements.name: Report Queue Prioritization
requirements.description: Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.

requirements.name: Item Use Metrics
requirements.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.

requirements.name: File Based Filtering
requirements.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report filters.

requirements.name: Notice Reports
requirements.description: The system must report pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

requirements.name: Pivot Table Output
requirements.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

requirements.name: Report Accuracy
requirements.description: Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.

requirements.name: Report Cancellation
requirements.description: Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.

requirements.name: Null Field Inclusion
requirements.description: Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.

requirements.name: Real Time Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting
requirements.description: The system must provide historical reporting through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.

requirements.name: Survey Name Filtering
requirements.description: Users must be able to select a survey by name for filtering, with the system resolving the name to its survey identifier internally.

requirements.name: MARC Row Consolidation
requirements.description: Reports must retrieve specified MARC fields and display them on one row even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.

requirements.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must report transactions for a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.

requirements.name: Collection Value Reports
requirements.description: The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.

requirements.name: Financial Compliance
requirements.description: Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

requirements.name: Financial Record Association
requirements.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.

requirements.name: High Balance Queries

requirements.description: The system must provide bills reports showing bill information as it existed at a past point in time.

requirements.name: Separate Item Dates
requirements.description: Item reports must expose last-edit date, last-circulation date, and check-in date and time as separate fields; last-edit date changes only when the item is edited, and renewal timestamps must not be treated as check-ins or edits.

requirements.name: Report Quick Access
requirements.description: The reporting interface must provide quick access to canned reports and templates, with hover or popup descriptions for report titles and templates.

requirements.name: Reporting Database Isolation
requirements.description: The system must provide a separate reporting database or replica when needed to isolate reporting workloads from the production database.

requirements.name: Background Report Processing
requirements.description: Long-running reports must execute in the background or through a queue without occupying the user interface.

requirements.name: Report Environment Help
requirements.description: The reporting system must provide integrated online help for its reporting interface.

requirements.name: Vendor And Library Integration
requirements.description: The system must provide a centralized service accepting input from and serving multiple branches as a single reporting source of truth.

requirements.name: Library Report Templates
requirements.description: The product must provide report templates needed by all consortium member branches for management reporting.

requirements.name: Director Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information.

requirements.name: Inventory Capacity Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide inventory and capacity reports for staff monitoring collections and operational capacity.

requirements.name: Management Reporting Scope
requirements.description: The reporting functionality must support management planning, evaluation, and oversight rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled by the OPAC and circulation client.

requirements.name: Report Data Requirements
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports and templates covering the management reporting needs of consortium branches.

glossary.definition: A physical library service point or other managed library location.
The organization or consortium that contains and manages multiple branches.
A physical or uncataloged material record managed by the system.
A person with a library account.
A generated presentation or export of queried system data.
A transaction involving checkout, check-in, renewal, hold activity, or related material use.
A patron request to reserve or obtain an item.
The operational condition assigned to an item or record, such as missing, damaged, or discard/weed.
The Online Public Access Catalog through which patrons access catalog, hold, and circulation functions.
The machine-readable cataloging data format used for bibliographic fields.
A title control number used to identify a bibliographic record.
An external union catalog used for bibliographic and holdings updates.
A comma-separated values file format used for data export.
A named security assignment that determines a user's permissions.
The enterprise system providing acquisitions, cataloging, circulation, and related library records.

requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library system or branch at the current or a historical date, including total items, new acquisitions, checked-in items, checked-out items, holds, adult fiction, and board books; checked-out items must count toward the total, and category groupings must be configurable by library system, such as fiction/non-fiction or format.
requirements.source_priority_note: D01 identifies the Material Volume Report as a key requirement

requirements.name: Acquisition Volume Trends
requirements.description: The system must use item acquisition dates to report material added during selectable periods, including the preceding 30, 60, or 90 days.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Overview
requirements.description: The system must provide authorized branch managers with an all-branch capacity view, allow drilldown to an individual branch, show capacity trends such as growth or shrinkage, and support comparison for up to 286 branches.

requirements.name: Branch Capacity Navigation
requirements.description: The capacity view must allow users to filter and sort branches by region, library type, and current load.

requirements.name: Capacity Data Export
requirements.description: The system must allow users to export capacity-view data in CSV format.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Analysis
requirements.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space, with views by branch and for the library system, selectable date ranges such as Q1 or Q2, collection percentages based on item counts, circulation percentages based on checkouts, and shelf-space estimates based on item dimensions or item count when dimensions are unavailable.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Comparisons
requirements.description: The system must show shelf-space analysis for branches side by side, including genre-and-format percentages for circulations, collection holdings, and shelf space, so users can identify differences and outliers.

requirements.name: Batch Item Transfers
requirements.description: Authorized staff must be able to transfer selected batches of items between branches and other destinations, including mobile libraries, outreach programs, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, by changing item locations or generating pull lists; the operation must process approximately 9.6 million items without excessive database locking.

requirements.name: Transfer Candidate Queries
requirements.description: Staff must be able to query for candidate items for transfer using criteria such as genre, collection area, and circulation inactivity, including items that have not circulated for six months.

requirements.name: Saved Transfer Queries
requirements.description: Staff must be able to save transfer-candidate queries for repeated use, including monthly reuse, and make saved queries available for reuse or sharing.

requirements.name: Transfer Item Selection
requirements.description: Staff must be able to manually select individual titles or items from transfer-query results before executing a transfer, such as selecting 25 items from 100 candidates.

requirements.name: Transfer Location Updates
requirements.description: The system must update the location field and associated item records for selected items moved to a new location.

requirements.name: Transfer Pull Lists
requirements.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer.

requirements.name: Transfer Reversion
requirements.description: The system must return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or configured event, including a status change to sold or returned or checkout at the destination.

requirements.name: Transfer Audit History
requirements.description: The system must record transfer history for each item, including enough history to determine patterns such as five transfers within one year.

requirements.name: Transfer Confirmation Preview
requirements.description: Before execution, the system must show a transfer preview containing the item count and source and destination locations and require staff confirmation.

requirements.name: Transfer Undo
requirements.description: Staff must be able to undo an erroneous transfer after it has been initiated or completed.

requirements.name: Transfer Role Permissions
requirements.description: The system must restrict transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.

requirements.name: Transit Label Generation
requirements.description: The system must generate printable barcode transit labels for transferred items.

requirements.name: Transfer Delay Alerts
requirements.description: The system must notify designated staff when a transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Reports
requirements.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.
requirements.source_priority_note: D05 calls the per-branch missing/damaged report crucial for accountability

requirements.name: Overdue Transit Report
requirements.description: The system must provide one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.

requirements.name: Purge Candidate Identification
requirements.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.

requirements.name: Batch Status Conversion
requirements.description: The system must provide a report or workflow for converting many selected items from one status to another in one batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.

requirements.name: Last Copy Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report items that are the only copy within a selected branch, library system, consortium, bibliographic work, or collection grouping, including deleted last copies where applicable, so catalogers can update WorldCat and avoid inappropriate deletion.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks this requirement critical; D15 marks the last copy report as critical

requirements.name: Orphan Record Deletion
requirements.description: The system must provide a quick method to delete volume entries with their associated copy entries and records with no attached items.

requirements.name: Protected Purge Reports
requirements.description: Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.

requirements.name: Confirmed Purge Deletion
requirements.description: The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.

requirements.name: Purge Audit Trail
requirements.description: The system must record who purged each record and when.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Logging
requirements.description: The system must record completed and denied deletion attempts, including record type, record ID, timestamp, user, user branch, library system, and, where required, deletion reason; deletion data must support counts and queries by branch, system, date range, user, record type, and highest-volume users.

requirements.name: Patron Report Filtering
requirements.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.

requirements.name: Configurable Age Ranges
requirements.description: Users must be able to configure age ranges separately for each patron report, including ranges such as 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 or 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.

requirements.name: Null Demographic Inclusion
requirements.description: Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
requirements.description: The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.

requirements.name: Inactive Report Scope
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must list or group results by configurable organizational scopes, including library system, home branch, and county, so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Outreach
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must include each patron's current mailing address and support CSV export for upload to an outreach system.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Exceptions
requirements.description: The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.

requirements.name: Scalable Inactive Reporting
requirements.description: For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.

requirements.name: Open-Hours Performance
requirements.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.

requirements.name: Server Platform Support
requirements.description: The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.

requirements.name: Client And Browser Access
requirements.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
requirements.description: The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.

requirements.name: Standards Compliant HTML
requirements.description: Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.

requirements.name: Environment Separation
requirements.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.

requirements.name: Configuration Migration
requirements.description: The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.

requirements.name: Role Based Access Control
requirements.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups; changing a role assignment must change permissions. Supported levels include Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

requirements.name: OPAC Preservation
requirements.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.

requirements.name: Process Documentation
requirements.description: The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

requirements.name: Online System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions and is accessible within the system and to screen readers.

requirements.name: Error Feedback
requirements.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.

requirements.name: Staff Authentication
requirements.description: The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.

requirements.name: Report Template Controls
requirements.description: Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.

requirements.name: Report Permission Administration
requirements.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.

requirements.name: Multi Record Query Designer
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, Boolean operators, and administrator control over tables, fields, and tool access.

requirements.name: Executive Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.

requirements.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
requirements.description: The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

requirements.name: Periodic Management Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide periodic reports for records with holds, items not checked out for a configurable period, item-level holds, invalid item types, in-transit items with holds, overdue transit, last copies, long call numbers, missing items, bibliographic records without items, and patrons with invalid home branches.

requirements.name: Query Criteria Display
requirements.description: Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.

requirements.name: Report Queue Monitoring
requirements.description: Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.

requirements.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
requirements.description: The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.

requirements.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
requirements.description: The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.

requirements.name: Uncataloged Material Control
requirements.description: The system must track uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books before catalog records exist, support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify usage, and include their transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

requirements.name: Collection And Capacity Analysis
requirements.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections, material use, branch capacity, patron demographics, staff workflow, financial transactions, and cross-branch performance for planning, evaluation, and oversight.

requirements.name: Consortium Statistical Reports
requirements.description: The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.

requirements.name: Data Quality Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.

requirements.name: Vendor Data Integration
requirements.description: Management processes must exchange standard-format data with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, and must continue to function when vendor data is unavailable at a branch.

requirements.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
requirements.description: Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.

requirements.name: OPAC Data Querying
requirements.description: Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.

requirements.name: Report Types
requirements.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.

requirements.name: Scheduled Canned Reports
requirements.description: Users must be able to run product-delivered canned reports using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data, select multiple canned reports, and combine their output in one document.

requirements.name: On Demand Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities.

requirements.name: Report Scheduling
requirements.description: Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.

requirements.name: Report Export Formats
requirements.description: Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system must deliver reports by email, allow users to enter recipients, and provide an address book for regularly used addresses.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Output
requirements.description: Reports must support comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage differences, and the corresponding month of the previous year.

requirements.name: Report Queue Prioritization
requirements.description: Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial

requirements.name: Item Use Metrics
requirements.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.

requirements.name: File Based Filtering
requirements.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report filters.

requirements.name: Notice Reports
requirements.description: The system must report pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

requirements.name: Pivot Table Output
requirements.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

requirements.name: Report Accuracy
requirements.description: Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.

requirements.name: Report Cancellation
requirements.description: Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.

requirements.name: Null Field Inclusion
requirements.description: Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.

requirements.name: Real Time Reporting
requirements.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting
requirements.description: The system must provide historical reporting through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.

requirements.name: Survey Name Filtering
requirements.description: Users must be able to select a survey by name for filtering, with the system resolving the name to its survey identifier internally.

requirements.name: MARC Row Consolidation
requirements.description: Reports must retrieve specified MARC fields and display them on one row even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.

requirements.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
requirements.description: The system must report transactions for a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.

requirements.name: Collection Value Reports
requirements.description: The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.

requirements.name: Financial Compliance
requirements.description: Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

requirements.name: Financial Record Association
requirements.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.

requirements.name: High Balance Queries
requirements.description: Staff must be able to query patron accounts with balances above a user-specified dollar amount.

requirements.name: Financial Data Updates
requirements.description: Authorized staff must be able to update financial information easily, and a payment made at a staff desk must be reflected immediately.

requirements.name: Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system must report patron balances by patron, home branch, and library system; fines and charges by period and charge type; waived fines by period and branch; and payments by period, collecting branch, payment channel, and payment type.

requirements.name: Payment Audit Ledger
requirements.description: The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.

requirements.name: Circulation Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-ins, checkouts, overdue items and patron contact information, circulation modifiers, categories, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home branch, age, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, and total circulation by type.

requirements.name: Item Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, created within a date range, missing, overdue, in transit, claimed returned, selected by use count, fines-stopped reason, weeding data, collection age, collection value, last-copy status, and batch status conversion.

requirements.name: Bibliographic Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide bibliographic reports for record counts, edited records, records added by user and branch, records without attached volumes or items, and records missing specified MARC fields.

requirements.name: Patron Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide patron reports for counts, additions by month, demographic categories, survey answers, expiration date, barred and inactive status, notes, and staff-account password-change and expiration dates, including counts by age, county, city, ZIP code, and home branch.

requirements.name: Hold Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide hold reports for purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans, unfilled holds, annual totals, and stale holds remaining beyond the permitted pickup period.

requirements.name: In House Use Reports
requirements.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use by month and cataloged in-house use.

requirements.name: Transit Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must report items in transit to a destination branch and items in transit by sending branch.

requirements.name: Bills Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for current patron bills, detailed payments, forgive/work/goods payments, voids, and aged debt with detailed aging periods.

requirements.name: Activity Cross Tabulation
requirements.description: Activity reports must show checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, cross-tabulated by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

requirements.name: Transaction Grouping
requirements.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days, preserve monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely, and group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, system, transaction type, and selected dimensions.

requirements.name: Checkin Method Counts
requirements.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, staff or user processing, and self-service.

requirements.name: Checkout Type Counts
requirements.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

requirements.name: Hold Placement Counts
requirements.description: The system must count hold requests and classify them by placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

requirements.name: Transaction Summary Reports
requirements.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts by patron, branch, selected branch groups, library system, and county, including checkout and hold subtotals and hold states such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.

requirements.name: Accounting Data Retention
requirements.description: The system must archive financial data according to state and local requirements and enforce applicable retention policies, including seven years of audit data where required.

requirements.name: Snapshot Bills Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide bills reports showing bill information as it existed at a past point in time.

requirements.name: Separate Item Dates
requirements.description: Item reports must expose last-edit date, last-circulation date, and check-in date and time as separate fields; last-edit date changes only when the item is edited, and renewal timestamps must not be treated as check-ins or edits.

requirements.description: The reporting interface must provide quick access to canned reports and templates, with hover or popup descriptions for report titles and templates.

requirements.name: Reporting Database Isolation
requirements.description: The system must provide a separate reporting database or replica when needed to isolate reporting workloads from the production database.

requirements.description: Long-running reports must execute in the background or through a queue without occupying the user interface.

requirements.description: The reporting system must provide integrated online help for its reporting interface.

requirements.description: The system must provide a centralized service accepting input from and serving multiple branches as a single reporting source of truth.

requirements.name: Library Report Templates
requirements.description: The product must provide report templates needed by all consortium member branches for management reporting.

requirements.name: Director Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information.

requirements.name: Inventory Capacity Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide inventory and capacity reports for staff monitoring collections and operational capacity.

messages.content:
You place candidate requirements that the consolidation step left unassigned. The user message is JSON with numbered "candidates" (index, name, description, source document) and the numbered current "requirements" (index, name, one-line description).

For every candidate return exactly one item, with no missing or duplicate indices:
- maps_to = the index of the requirement that already covers it (a tester would write one test for both, or the candidate is only a detail of that requirement) and new = false; or
- new = true and maps_to = null when no current requirement covers it.
Map only when the coverage is genuine; a shared topic is not coverage.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

added.name: Save Reusable Queries
added.description: The system must allow staff to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting activities.

added.name: Select Query Results Manually
added.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative actions.

messages.content:
You read one input document against the current requirements list. The user message is JSON with the document (id, path, full text) and the FULL list of current requirements, numbered by index (index, name, description).

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below.   "text": "================================================================================
PINES REPORTS WORKING GROUP - SECOND MEETING MINUTES
================================================================================

Date: July 20, 2009
Time: 9:30 AM - 12:00 PM EST
Location: Georgia Public Library Service, Conference Room A, Atlanta, GA
Meeting Type: Regular Working Group Meeting

ATTENDEES:
- Katherine Gregory (PINES Services Specialist) - Chair
- LaToya Davidson (Twin Lakes Library System) - Library Director
- Jennifer Durham (Statesboro Regional Library System) - Assistant Library Director
- Dana Peeler (Ohoopee Regional Library) - Systems Librarian
- Susan Sexton-Cooley (Sara Hightower Regional Library) - Assistant Library Director
- George Tuttle (Piedmont Regional Library) - Assistant Library Director
- Chris Sharp (PINES Staff Facilitator)

ABSENTEES: None

1. CALL TO ORDER AND REVIEW OF ACTION ITEMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine called the meeting to order at 9:35 AM.

Action items from the March 15 meeting:
  - Interviews with staff: COMPLETED (all members submitted reports)
  - Circulation of Galecia Group draft: COMPLETED
  - Technical subcommittee meeting: SCHEDULED for June 30 (see below)

2. INTERVIEW FINDINGS SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each member presented a summary of their interview findings:

LaToya Davidson (Twin Lakes): Spoke with 3 branch managers. Key themes:
  - Inventory and capacity reports are used daily
  - Financial report needs are understood at the director level
  - Need for cross-branch comparison reports

Jennifer Durham (Statesboro): Spoke with 2 branch managers and 1 director.
  Key themes:
  - Report queue visibility is important
  - Board/executive reports need to be pre-defined
  - Data quality reports are needed

Dana Peeler (Ohoopee): Spoke with 1 branch manager. Key themes:
  - Staff login needs (card swipe) - already discussed via email
  - In-transit item reports are critical for delivery coordination
  - Missing/damaged item reports are needed per branch

Susan Sexton-Cooley (Sara Hightower): Spoke with 1 branch manager. Key themes:
  - Weeding reports are frequently used
  - Shelf space utilization reports are important
  - Demographic analysis for program planning

George Tuttle (Piedmont): Spoke with 1 branch manager and 1 IT staff.
  Key themes:
  - Technical constraints (server OS, browser support)
  - User permissions and role-based access
  - Accessibility requirements

3. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This section was led by Dana Peeler and George Tuttle, drawing on input from
their interviews.

OE-1: Management Processes must support the needs of a large, multiple-system
      library consortium. Specifically, the system must support a library
      consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations,
      purchasing and processing over 900,000 items per year. It is highly
      desirable that searches and reports can be processed during open hours
      without disrupting other system functions.

      [Discussion: George noted that Evergreen already handles this scale.
      The concern is about report processing during peak hours. We need
      background processing/queuing to prevent report generation from slowing
      down the circulation client.]

OE-2: Management Processes shall operate on a Linux or Solaris server.
      [Consensus: Both Linux and Solaris are acceptable. Most PINES
      installations use Linux, but some larger systems use Solaris.]

OE-3: Management Processes shall be accessible through a web-browser or a
      Windows-compatible client.
      [Discussion: This is critical - some libraries prefer browser-based
      access (no client install), others prefer the dedicated client for
      better performance.]

OE-4: If web-browser based, Management Processes shall be accessible through
      Microsoft Internet Explorer (v.6.0 and later) and Mozilla Firefox
      (v.2.0 and later).
      [Discussion: We need to support both IE and Firefox because different
      libraries standardize on different browsers. IE 6 is still common in
      our library environments, even though it's old.]

OE-5: Management Processes shall be accessible with screen-reading software,
      screen-magnification software, and other software programs designed to
      increase accessibility.
      [Discussion: Susan emphasized this is a legal requirement for public
      institutions. We need to support JAWS, NVDA, ZoomText, and other
      assistive technologies. Section 508 compliance is mandatory.]

4. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This section was led by George Tuttle, drawing on his IT interview.

CO-1: Management Processes shall use a fully relational database back-end.
      [Discussion: Evergreen already uses PostgreSQL. We need to ensure our
      reporting layer works properly with the relational structure.]

CO-2: Management Processes shall produce standards-compliant HTML.
      [Discussion: All web output needs to be valid HTML. This affects report
      display, help system, and any web-based UI components.]

CO-3: Management Processes shall provide a development and training environment
      with the ability to migrate configurations to a production environment.
      [Discussion: Katherine noted that Evergreen development follows this
      pattern - developers have separate environments. We need to make sure
      report templates and configurations can be exported/imported.]

CO-4: User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups
      and/or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups,
      and arbitrary staff groups.
      [Discussion: George confirmed this is essential. We need flexible
      role-based access control.]

CO-5: These requirements shall not constrain functionality or features of the
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module.
      [Discussion: The management processes are separate from the public-
      facing catalog. Changes to management reporting should not affect
      patron access.]

5. USER DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine led a discussion on user documentation needs:

UD-1: The software developer shall provide complete data specifications for
      authority records, bibliographic records, order records, item records,
      hold/request records, and other records maintained or accessed by
      Management Processes.

      [Discussion: Staff need to understand the data structures to write
      effective queries. Data dictionaries are essential.]

UD-2: The software developer shall provide a thorough high-level description
      of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export,
      validation of bibliographic records against internal and external
      authority sources, and standard reports.

      [Discussion: Process flow documentation helps staff understand how
      data moves through the system.]

UD-3: The system shall provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help
      system in HTML that describes and illustrates all system functions.

      [Discussion: Context-sensitive help is critical. Staff shouldn't have
      to leave the system to find documentation.]

UD-4: The system shall provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback
      and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for Local and Global
      System Administrators from the front-end interface.

      [Discussion: When reports fail, staff need to understand why. Error
      messages should be meaningful.]

6. ASSUMPTIONS AND DEPENDENCIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation
      System.
      [Discussion: This means we can rely on the infrastructure being
      enterprise-grade. Evergreen is that system for PINES.]

AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept
      input and provide services to multiple locations.
      [Discussion: Centralization enables consistent reporting but requires
      good network connectivity.]

DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an
      enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and
      Cataloging modules.
      [Discussion: The data we report on comes from the ILS. We don't manage
      acquisitions or cataloging ourselves.]

DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via
      published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files
      (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).
      [Discussion: Some libraries use external vendors for certain functions.
      Our reporting needs to handle data from these sources too.]

DE-3: Management Processes interact with a patron interface, also known as an
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC).
      [Discussion: Patron data (holds, circulation) is created in the OPAC.
      Our reports need to query this data.]

7. REPORTS WORKING GROUP MISSION REVIEW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Katherine reviewed the working group's mission:

  Reports Working Group Mission:
  1. Document optimal Reports functionality within a future Evergreen release
     and develop a list of requirements.
  2. Become the Reports testing group, through which all new Reports development
     would be filtered.
  3. Compile a list of reports needed for an Executive Reports Interface.
  4. Determine and create templates needed for all PINES libraries.

All members agreed the mission is still accurate and relevant.

8. ACTION ITEMS AND NEXT STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - Technical subcommittee meeting: June 30, 2009 (Katherine to send agenda)
  - Complete draft of requirements document: by September 1, 2009
  - Katherine to circulate consolidated requirements list
  - George and Dana to draft technical architecture section
  - All members to continue gathering detailed report requirements

Meeting adjourned at 12:00 PM.

Minutes prepared by: Katherine Gregory, PINES Services Specialist
Minutes distributed: July 22, 2009"

DRAFT SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION

FOR THE MANAGEMENT PROCESSES
OF AN
INTEGRATED LIBRARY SYSTEM

================================================================================

Prepared by:
Lori Ayre & Lucien Kress
Galecia Group
Consulting for Libraries and Cultural Heritage Organizations

Version: 1.0 DRAFT (for review)
Date: January 27, 2009
Status: Internal Draft - Circulating for Comment

================================================================================
TABLE OF CONTENTS
================================================================================

1. Executive Summary
2. Product Perspective
3. User Characteristics
4. Operating Environment Requirements
5. Design and Implementation Constraints
6. User Documentation Requirements
7. Assumptions and Dependencies
8. Functional Requirements - General Management Tools
9. Functional Requirements - Demographics
10. Functional Requirements - Inventory Control
11. Functional Requirements - Patron Records
12. Functional Requirements - Transaction Records
