================================================================================
1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This document presents a draft set of requirements for the management and
reporting processes of an Integrated Library System (ILS). These requirements
were developed for King County Library System (KCLS) in Washington State but
are believed to be applicable to many large, urban, multiple-branch,
centralized library systems.

The purpose of this document is to provide a comprehensive set of requirements
that can guide the development of reporting and management tools within an ILS.
The requirements cover functional aspects only; data structures and user
interfaces will require further specification and development using an
iterative, prototype-oriented methodology.

King County serves over 2.3 million residents across 49 libraries with an
annual circulation of approximately 8 million items. The system maintains
over 4 million bibliographic records and serves over 650,000 active borrower
accounts.

NOTE: This is a DRAFT document. Requirements are subject to change based on
feedback from stakeholders and additional analysis. Items marked [*] are
considered high priority by KCLS but may need adjustment for other systems.

================================================================================
2. PRODUCT PERSPECTIVE
================================================================================

The Management Processes component of an ILS provides the tools needed for
library administrators, managers, and staff to analyze operations, manage
collections, and make data-driven decisions. This component operates as part
of a larger enterprise-level Library Automation System.

The Management Processes are consolidated at a central location and accept
input from and provide services to multiple library locations. They rely on
the data structures and functionality of the broader ILS, including Acquisitions
and Cataloging modules.

The current specification presupposes the general functionality of an ILS and
specifies only those requirements that directly or indirectly relate to
management activities. While the requirements were developed specifically for
King County, they are expected to be suitable for many similar library systems.

The Management Processes facilitate the management of Library services,
programs, and policies. Specifically, the Management Processes support:

  - Analyzing the Library collection and its use by patrons.
  - Analyzing branch capacity and optimal distribution of the collection.
  - Analyzing the demographics and interests of patrons.
  - Analyzing staff productivity and workflow.
  - Tracking and verifying financial transactions.

================================================================================
3. USER CHARACTERISTICS
================================================================================

The following user types have been identified:

* Patron: A person utilizing the resources of a library, either as a member
  of the public with a library card or as a member of the public without a
  card. Patrons may interact with the system through the OPAC.

* Staff: Employees of the library system who are involved in designing and
  providing services to the public. This includes circulation staff, reference
  staff, and specialized staff.

* Local System Administrators: Individuals (typically library managers) who
  oversee library processes and have elevated permissions within the system.
  They can configure local settings and run system reports.

* Library Managers: Individuals who supervise organizational units and provide
  input to the design and implementation of library services. They use reports
  for planning and evaluation.

* Library Administrators: Senior leadership who plan and direct library services
  and priorities. They require aggregated, high-level reports for strategic
  planning and board presentations.

* Global System Administrator: The individual(s) who manage the ILS at the
  consortium level, implementing software changes and configurations, and
  generating statistical reports for the entire system.

================================================================================
4. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

OE-1: The system must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million
      annual circulations, and purchasing/processing over 900,000 items per year.
      It is highly desirable that searches and reports can be processed during
      open hours without disrupting other system functions.
      [* High Priority]

OE-2: The system must operate on a Linux or Solaris server environment.
      [* High Priority]

OE-3: The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible
      client.
      [* High Priority]

OE-4: If web-browser based, the system must be accessible through Microsoft
      Internet Explorer (version 6.0 and later) and Mozilla Firefox (version
      2.0 and later).
      [* Medium Priority]

OE-5: The system must be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-
      magnification software, and other assistive technology programs designed
      to increase accessibility.
      [* High Priority]

================================================================================
5. DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS
================================================================================

CO-1: The system must use a fully relational database back-end. [* High Priority]

CO-2: The system must produce standards-compliant HTML output for web-based
      components.
      [* High Priority]

CO-3: The system must provide a development and training environment with the
      ability to migrate configurations to a production environment.
      [* Medium Priority]

CO-4: User rights and privileges will be controlled through security groups and
      or "roles" that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and
      arbitrary staff groups.
      [* High Priority]

CO-5: These requirements must not constrain functionality or features of the
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC) module.
      [* High Priority]

================================================================================
6. USER DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

UD-1: The developer must provide complete data specifications for authority
      records, bibliographic records, order records, item records, hold/request
      records, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management
      Processes.
      [* High Priority]

UD-2: The developer must provide a thorough high-level description of major
      processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation
      of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources,
      and standard reports.
      [* Medium Priority]

UD-3: The system must provide an online, hierarchical, and cross-linked help
      system in HTML that describes and illustrates all system functions.
      [* High Priority]

UD-4: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback,
      and shall allow low-level query-specific feedback for Local and Global
      System Administrators from the front-end interface.
      [* Medium Priority]

================================================================================
7. ASSUMPTIONS AND DEPENDENCIES
================================================================================

AS-1: Management Processes are part of an enterprise-level Library Automation
      System.

DE-1: Management Processes rely on the data structures and functionality of an
      enterprise-level Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and
      Cataloging modules.

AS-2: Management Processes are consolidated at a central location, and accept
      input and provide services to multiple locations.

DE-2: Management Processes interface with a variety of vendor websites, via
      published APIs and/or automated transfer of standard-format data files
      (e.g., USMARC21, EDIFACT).

DE-3: Management Processes interact with a patron interface, also known as an
      Online Public Access Catalog (OPAC).

================================================================================
8. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL MANAGEMENT TOOLS
================================================================================

[*] = High Priority item

8.1 Staff Login
The system should support streamlined methods of logging into terminals. For
example, a staff member could swipe a card (like an RFID employee badge) to
log in, or alternatively use individual login credentials (username and
password). The system should not REQUIRE card-based login - traditional
username/password should also be available as a fallback.

8.2 Report Templates
System administrators should be able to create report templates that are
available to staff. These templates should be runnable as-is or modifiable
for individual needs. Changes to templates should not compromise the accuracy
of results. Administrators should be able to limit which filters and display
fields can be altered, to certify a dependable output.

For example, front-line staff could set a call number range for a weeding
report or add/remove display fields from a pick list, but they should not be
able to alter the template to display deleted items.

8.3 Report Permissions
The system should provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit
who can create and clone reports. All permissions should be easy to administer.
System administrators should be able to create shared folders to allow or
disallow staff from running specific reports, and/or to run ad hoc reports on
specific sets of data.

8.4 Query Tool
The system should provide a user-friendly interface for designing queries
against all record types (bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial).
Staff should be able to:
  - Select fields to query
  - Select values from a picklist of possible values
  - Select regular expressions from a drop-down menu
  - Use a full range of Boolean operators

Administrators should control staff access to tables and fields.

8.5 Board Reports / Executive Reports
The system should provide pre-defined reports for consumption by library boards
and other external consumers. These should include basic statistics like those
required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid.

Activity reports should indicate traffic and volume of use, displaying
statistics on check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. It
should be possible to cross-tabulate per terminal, per branch, per library
system, per hour, per patron age range, per patron type, and per patron
location.

8.6 Transaction Data Archiving
Transactions should be archived in a form that protects patron privacy as
defined by State Law, while providing useful demographic statistics.

8.7 Periodic Report Examples
Examples of periodic reports include:
  - Bibliographic records with holds
  - Items that have not been checked out in X days
  - Item-level holds
  - Items with invalid item type
  - In-transit items with outstanding hold
  - Items that have been in-transit for more than X days
  - Items that are the last copy in the system
  - Items with a long call number
  - Missing items
  - Bibliographic records with no item records
  - Patrons with invalid home library

8.8 Query Selections Display
The system should provide the query selections along with the results, so users
can see what criteria were used to generate the report.

8.9 Report Queue
Staff should be able to see where their report is in the queue of reports
waiting to run.

8.10 Canned Report Examples
The system must be able to support the reporting definitions as described in
the attached report examples (see Appendix A).

8.11 Fine-Grained Reporting Requirements
The system must be able to support the fine-grained reports requirements as
described in the attached specification (see Appendix B).

================================================================================
9. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - DEMOGRAPHICS
================================================================================

9.1 Patron Behavior and Use Analysis
The system should produce statistics that can be used to understand and predict
patron behavior and use of materials. For example:
  - How quickly is a particular book returned, on average?
  - How likely is a particular book to be renewed?
  - What percent of check-outs at a particular branch are renewals?

9.2 Demographic Statistics
The system should produce useful demographic statistics, including transactions
by geographical regions, age ranges, etc. The data used to produce these
statistics must be anonymized - information that could be used to identify a
patron is deleted.

================================================================================
10. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - INVENTORY CONTROL
================================================================================

10.1 Material Volume Report
Ability to report on the volume of material in a given library at any point in
time, based on new acquisitions, items on the shelf, and items out in
circulation. The report should allow breaking down volume in categories such
as: total items in library, number of holds, number of adult fiction, number
of board books, etc.

10.2 System Capacity Interface
The system should provide an interface showing the capacity of all branches.

10.3 Shelf Space Report
For each genre and format of material, ability to compare:
  - The percentage of total circulations
  - The percentage of the collection
  - The percentage of total shelf space

The report should be able to run per library and per system.

10.4 Uncataloged Material
Ability to control inventory of uncataloged material, such as paperback books
and children's board books. Support needed for:
  - Quick distribution
  - Minimal branch labor
  - Ability to identify how the material is being used

Ability to count transactions and include in circulation statistics and
reports.

10.5 Item Transfer Utility
System should provide a utility for transferring batches of items between
branches. Uses include: moving books into a mobile library, an outreach program
collection, or a "just-in-time" warehouse.

The utility should include:
  - Ability to query for candidate materials
  - Ability to save queries for repeated use
  - Ability to manually select titles from query results
  - Ability to change records of selected items to move to new location
  - Mechanisms for moving items: changing location field, generating pull lists
  - Ability to revert items to original location after a set period of time

10.6 Missing and Damaged Items Report
The system should provide reports of missing and damaged items per branch.

10.7 In-Transit Items Report
The system should generate a list of items that have been in-transit for more
than X days (X configurable), per branch and per system. The report should
merge the transit-to and transit-from into one report for ease of front-line
staff use.

10.8 Item Record Purging
The system should provide a utility and reports for identifying item records
to purge, based on customizable criteria such as:
  - An item has been in status "missing" for more than X months
  - An item has status "discard/weed"

The system should have a report to assist in the conversion of items from one
status to another. The system should provide a last copy report that singles
out a library system's last copies, to assist catalogers who need to edit
WorldCat entries. The system should provide a quick effective method of
deleting volume entries along with copy entries, as well as records with no
items attached.

10.9 Deletions Tracking
Ability to count and track record deletions (e.g., item records, patron records)
per location and per system.

================================================================================
11. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - PATRON RECORDS
================================================================================

11.1 Patron Characteristics
Queries and reports can be limited or grouped by various patron characteristics,
including:
  - age range
  - zip code
  - county of residence
  - home branch
  - patron type
  - preferred language

11.2 Inactive Patrons Report
The system should generate a list of patrons with no circulation or electronic
activity in the last X days (X configurable). The list should be configurable
to System, Home Library, County, etc.

================================================================================
12. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - TRANSACTION RECORDS
================================================================================

12.1 Transaction History Maintenance
Transaction history is maintained for X days (X is configurable). Monthly and
annual aggregate information is maintained indefinitely.

12.2 Backroom Statistics Examples
Transactions can be grouped by hour, terminal, branch, and system. Transactions
include check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, patron registrations, etc., and
can be queried by all transactions or by type of transaction.

12.3 Types of Check-In
The system counts all types of check-in individually and cumulatively:
  - book-drop
  - by terminal
  - by user or self-service

12.4 Types of Check-Out
The system counts all types of check-out individually and cumulatively:
  - staff check-out
  - self check-out
  - staff renewal
  - self checkout renewal
  - online renewal
  - OPAC renewal

12.5 Holds and Locations
The system counts all hold requests, including how the hold was placed:
  - at a staff desk
  - at a public computer inside the library
  - remotely

12.6 Transactions Report
The system can generate a report of transactions (holds placed, holds filled,
and check-outs) per patron, per library, per selected group of libraries,
per system, per county. The system displays the number of check-outs and
placed holds per patron. Holds are subtotaled by type, e.g., active, frozen,
and frozen-until holds.

================================================================================
13. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS - FINANCIAL RECORDS
================================================================================

13.1 Value of Items Report
The system can generate a report of the value of items (based on data in item
record) in the entire collection or a portion. Example: staff can obtain value
of all items with status of longoverdue, or value of all DVDs in children's
collection, or value of entire collection.

13.2 Standard Accounting Practice and Auditing Requirements
All reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practice
and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

13.3 Financial Data (Patrons)
Fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions are attached to patron
and item records. System tracks fines waived and payments made per library.
Financial information can be updated easily. As an example, a staff user can
easily query patron accounts with balances greater than X dollars.

13.4 Financial Reports
The system provides financial reports including:
  - patron account balances by patron, home library, and system
  - fines and charges accrued per time period (e.g., last twelve months, YTD,
    last month) and per type of charge (overdue fines, damaged item charges,
    lost item charges, etc.)
  - fines waived per time period and per branch
  - payments made per time period and per payment method (e.g., staff desk,
    self-check station, OPAC)

13.5 Financial Audit Trail
The system maintains a ledger of patron payments, including which charges
payments are applied to, to facilitate reconciliation.

15. FINE-GRAINED REPORTING REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

This appendix contains detailed requirements for the reporting interface and
functionality.

15.1 Three Interfaces
Three interfaces are needed:
  a) Canned reports - generic reports set to run by the individual either ASAP
     or recurring
  b) Noncanned or On Demand Reports - preset but have the ability to edit
     selection criteria and display options
  c) Open Template Reporting - all attributes associated with circulation,
     items, patrons, bills, and bibs to select from for filtering and display

15.2 Canned Reports Details
Canned reports are generic reports set to run by the individual either ASAP or
recurring. There should be a certain set of templates that are pre-written and
delivered with the product. Will have the ability for it to run by yesterday's
data, last week's, last month's, or last year's. Canned reports can be checked
off from a list to run at the same time and will be viewed within one document.

15.3 On Demand Reports
On Demand Reports would be for pre-selected criteria but for things like
maintenance reports or collections development and would be set to run on demand.

15.4 Open Template Reporting
Open template would have all attributes associated with say circulation,
patrons, items, bills, and bibs to select from for filtering and the same
attributes for displaying.

15.5 Quick Access Interface
- Ability to hover over each title of canned report/template with pop-up box
  with description
- Check off any part of data you want
- Ability to select Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly
- Output would be in Excel, HTML, and CSV format
- Ability to enter email addresses for report to be sent to - would be great to
  have an address book of regularly used addresses
- Ability to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections
  as well as editing the email addresses
- Ability to determine the output results in a way such that a result could have
  one column for last month's circs, another for previous month's circ, a percent
  difference column, previous year's month column, a percent difference from
  last month to last year's month column
- The system provides a report to assist in the batch conversion of statuses
- Ability to edit canned report for display purposes such as adding shelving
  location as a display
- Ability to add more canned reports via permission level
- Ability to get a list of items deleted that was the last copy owned by the
  library system in order to update WorldCat
- Ability to prioritize certain types of reports so they will pop to the top of
  the queue over resource-consuming reports
- Ability to have a total use count on items as well as a use count broken down
  by usage date range such as an FY use count or monthly use count
- Ability to retrieve total circ including checkouts, renewals, and noncats
  with a breakdown displaying those circ types
- Ability to upload a text file such as barcodes or TCN to use for filtering
  on a report
- Ability to run reports for pre-overdue, overdue, and holds notices sent
- Pivot table output
- Tested and proven output
- Ability to cancel a report that has already been scheduled to run or is
  currently running
- All nulls and blank fields must be included in the results no matter what is
  being filtered or displayed
- Ability to have real time reporting
- Ability to have historical reporting - a reporting warehouse such that data
  can be acquired on a given date or date range
- Selection criteria is clearly defined
- Report results would include the date selection criteria at the top or bottom
  to quickly see date range selected along with the name of the report
- Ability to select the survey name and not have to enter the survey id for
  filtering
- Ability to run a report on deleted items that were the last copy in the facility
- Ability to pull MARC record fields so that they appear on a single row of data
- Ability to run a report on transactions that occurred on x date and time on x
  workstation or by x staff

Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

EVERGREEN ILS - REPORTING MODULE OVERVIEW
================================================================================
Reference Document
Version: 1.4.0.4
Date: March 15, 2009
Source: Evergreen Official Documentation & PINES IT Department Analysis

================================================================================
1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW
================================================================================

Evergreen is an open-source Integrated Library System (ILS) originally
developed by the Georgia Public Library Service for use in PINES. The current
version in production at PINES is 1.4.0.4.

This document provides an overview of the existing reporting capabilities
within Evergreen, along with identified gaps and limitations that have driven
the need for enhanced Management Processes reporting.

PINES currently operates Evergreen across 286 library locations, serving
approximately 3.5 million patrons with a collection of 9.6 million items.

================================================================================
2. EXISTING REPORTING COMPONENTS
================================================================================

2.1 REPORT WRITER INTERFACE
Evergreen includes a report writer that allows staff to create custom reports
using a web-based interface. Key features:

- Drag-and-drop field selection
- Basic filtering and sorting
- Multiple output formats (CSV, HTML, sometimes Excel)
- Ability to save and reuse report definitions

Limitations:
- Complex queries are difficult to construct
- No Boolean operators (AND/OR) beyond simple filters
- Limited field selection (not all database fields are available)
- No regular expression support
- No query queue visibility

2.2 CANNED REPORTS
Pre-defined reports available in Evergreen 1.4.0.4:

CIRCULATION:
- Checkout Count
- Renewals Count
- Non-Cataloged Count
- Circulation Count by Shelving Location

ITEMS:
- Items Added Count
- Items Deleted Count
- Items Currently Checked Out
- Items Overdue by X Days
- List of Items with Missing Status

BIB RECORDS:
- Bib Records Count
- Bib Records with No Volumes Attached

PATRONS:
- Patron Count
- Patron Count by Home Library

BILLS:
- Bills Currently Owed by Patrons
- Detailed Payments Received
- Aged Debt

2.3 REPORT SCHEDULING
Some reports can be scheduled to run at regular intervals (daily, weekly,
monthly). However, scheduling options are limited:

- No hourly scheduling
- No ability to check multiple reports to run at the same time
- No email delivery (reports can only be downloaded from the web interface)

2.4 PERMISSIONS
Current permission model:
- Staff can run any report they can access
- No fine-grained control over who can create vs. run reports
- No shared folders concept
- No ability to limit which filters staff can use

================================================================================
3. REPORTABLE DATA STRUCTURES
================================================================================

3.1 RECORD TYPES
The following record types are available for reporting:

- bibliographic_record: Title, author, ISBN, publication info, subjects, etc.
- item: Call number, barcode, location (copy location), status, etc.
- patron: Name, address, library, patron type, etc.
- action_circulation: Checkout, checkout, renewal, holds, etc.
- action_hold: Hold requests
- money: Fines, payments, credits, etc.
- actor: Staff accounts and permissions

3.2 KEY RELATIONSHIPS
- bibliographic_record -> item (through asset.copy)
- item -> action.circulation (through circulation transactions)
- patron -> action.circulation (through patron_id)
- patron -> money (through debt records)
- actor -> action.circulation (through librarian link)

3.3 AVAILABLE FIELDS (SAMPLE)
For bibliographic_record:
- id, fingerprint, scan_timestamp, record_type,
  edition, language, ISBN, ISSN, UPC, EAN, publisher_name,
  publication_date, place_of_publication, physical_description

For item:
- id, barcode, label, copy_number, location (copy_location),
  status (acq status), circ_modifier, call_number,
  purchase_date, purchase_price, shelving_location,
  age_hold_protect, reserve_id

For patron:
- id, barcode, opac (visible fields), family_lib (home library),
  usr_grp (patron type), em (email),
  address lines, city, state, zip (postal code),
  birth_date, create_date

================================================================================
4. IDENTIFIED GAPS AND LIMITATIONS
================================================================================

The following reporting capabilities are MISSING from Evergreen 1.4.0.4 or
are severely limited:

4.1 MISSING REPORT TYPES
- Circulation Count by Circ Modifier (partially available)
- Circulation Count by Dewey (not available)
- Circulation Count by MARC fields (not available)
- Circulation Count by Circ Location broken down by Patron County (not available)
- Circulation Count by Age Demographic (not available)
- Items Edited Count (not available)
- List of Items by Fines Stopped Reason (not available)
- Items more than XX days overdue with patron contact info (not available)
- List of Items with specific Total Use Count (not available)
- Last Copy Report (partially available, needs enhancement)
- List of Items by Creation Date Range (not available)
- Claims Returned report (not available)
- Weeding report with date of last circulation (partially available)
- Age of collection by call number (not available)
- Price value of collection by call number (not available)
- Bib Records Edited Count (not available)
- Bib Records Added by user by library Count (not available)
- Bib Records missing specific MARC fields (not available)
- Patron Count by Age Demographic (not available)
- Patron Count by County (not available)
- Patron Count by County, City, & Zip Code (not available)
- Voter Survey Responses (not available)
- List of Patrons with inactive status (not available)
- Staff Accounts with date of last password change (not available)
- Holds Purchase Alert (not available)
- Unfilled Holds (not available)
- Stale Holds (not available)
- Aged Debt detailed report (partially available, needs enhancement)

4.2 MISSING FEATURES
- No report queue visibility (staff can't see where their report is in queue)
- No ability to prioritize certain types of reports
- No ability to cancel a running report
- No pivot table output
- No real-time reporting (all reports are run on current data)
- No historical reporting warehouse
- No ability to select Run ASAP, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly
- No email delivery of reports
- No address book for report delivery
- No ability to upload text files for filtering (barcodes, TCNs)
- No selection criteria display in report results
- No ability to edit canned report display options
- No quick access interface with pop-up descriptions
- No hover tooltips for report titles

4.3 MISSING ARCHITECTURAL ELEMENTS
- No separate reporting database/replica (reports run on production database)
- No background processing for long-running reports
- No report template management system
- No fine-grained permissions for reports
- No development/training environment separation
- No configuration migration between environments
- No accessibility support for report interface
- No online help system integrated with reports

4.4 FINE-GRAINED REQUIREMENTS NOT MET
Several fine-grained reporting requirements from the King County specification
are not met by Evergreen 1.4.0.4:

- Three interfaces (canned, on-demand, open template) - only basic canned exists
- Open Template Reporting - does not exist
- Real time reporting - does not exist
- Historical reporting warehouse - does not exist
- Snapshot bills report going back in time - does not exist
- Last edit date not including last circulation - does not exist
- Ability to indicate last circulation date - not available as separate field
- Checkin Date/time not including renewals - checkin and renewal timestamps
  are stored together
- All nulls and blank fields included in results - current system may filter
  some nulls

================================================================================
5. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

Evergreen 1.4.0.4 provides basic reporting capabilities but has significant
gaps in several areas. The management processes reporting system needs to:

1. Expand the available report types to cover all identified gaps
2. Implement fine-grained permissions and template management
3. Add report queue visibility and status indicators
4. Provide multiple output formats and scheduling options
5. Implement accessibility compliance
6. Separate reporting from production operations
7. Provide a development/training environment with migration capability

This analysis was conducted by the PINES IT Department and is based on
review of the Evergreen codebase version 1.4.0.4 and production usage patterns
observed in the PINES environment.

================================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT
================================================================================"

Return two lists:

1. supports: the indices of every requirement this document states or clearly implies, per the definition below. Topic overlap is not support: the document must ask for, or describe as needed, what the requirement says the system must do or be; supporting a part of a requirement counts. Use only indices from the list; an empty list is fine.

2. missed: requirements stated or clearly implied in this document that no listed requirement covers, even in other words or at a different level of detail. An empty list is the expected answer when the list is complete. A detail of a listed capability is not missed; ignore it. Options, fields, filters, sort orders, display rules, thresholds and similar details of one capability belong inside that capability's description, never in a separate requirement. Several distinct capabilities are never one requirement, even when they come from the same document, thread or stakeholder; sharing a topic is not a reason to merge. Only explicit asks or clearly implied needs count. An open question, a complaint without a request, an aside, or a remark about what people do is not a requirement, and you add no capability the source does not mention (for example no extra operators or options for a query tool). Skip small talk and project process (meeting schedules, who should be interviewed, testing and QA process, assumptions about the team). Documentation and training that a source states as requirements of the software or product (for example user documentation items in a draft specification) are requirements and are kept. Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). The description states only what the system must do or be: no provenance (which document, who said it) and no priority prose. Source priority signals go in source_priority_note instead: when a source marks the item with an explicit priority marker (for example [*] or "High") or calls it critical, mandatory, legally required or non-negotiable, write a short note naming the document id (for example "D10 marks this High; D06 calls it critical"); otherwise null. A note describes only its own item: never attach a signal a source gives for a different capability.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

Priority scale:
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Hard rule, applied first: if an item's source_priority_note reports an explicit priority marker in a specification document (for example [*] or High in a draft SRS), a source calling the item critical, or wording that it is legally required, mandatory, non-negotiable or a compliance obligation, the priority is High and the justification names that source. An individual's emphasis in an e-mail or interview ("crucial", "essential", "we really need") is evidence for the judgment below, not a trigger.

Judge every other item by how central it is to the system's purpose, how many source documents ask for it (source_doc_ids) and whether the system can work without it, calibrated against the fixed requirements:
- Medium is not a default: clear value without urgency is Medium; nice-to-have and single-stakeholder conveniences are Low. Aim for a defensible spread across the three levels.
- A feature mentioned once in passing by one person is not High on its own, nor is a requirement that only exists as a thin list heading (for example "provide canned reports").
- A sub-feature of a report or utility is never higher than the report or utility.

    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 31,
   "name": "Patron Report Filtering",
   "description": "The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D08 calls these reports essential"
  },
  {
   "index": 32,
   "name": "Configurable Age Ranges",
   "description": "Users must be able to configure age ranges separately for each patron report, including ranges such as 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 or 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 33,
   "name": "Null Demographic Inclusion",
   "description": "Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 34,
   "name": "Inactive Patron Reporting",
   "description": "The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 35,
   "name": "Inactive Report Scope",
   "description": "The inactive patron report must list or group results by configurable organizational scopes, including library system, home branch, and county, so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 36,
   "name": "Inactive Patron Outreach",
   "description": "The inactive patron report must include each patron's current mailing address and support CSV export for upload to an outreach system.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 37,
   "name": "Inactive Patron Exceptions",
   "description": "The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 38,
   "name": "Scalable Inactive Reporting",
   "description": "For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 39,
   "name": "Consortium Scale",
   "description": "The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D02",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks OE-1 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 40,
   "name": "Open-Hours Performance",
   "description": "Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 41,
   "name": "Server Platform Support",
   "description": "The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks OE-2 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 42,
   "name": "Client And Browser Access",
   "description": "The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical"
  },
  {
   "index": 43,
   "name": "Assistive Technology Access",
   "description": "The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory"
  },
  {
   "index": 44,
   "name": "Relational Database Support",
   "description": "The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks CO-1 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 45,
   "name": "Standards Compliant HTML",
   "description": "Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks CO-2 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 46,
   "name": "Environment Separation",
   "description": "The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks CO-3 Medium Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 47,
   "name": "Configuration Migration",
   "description": "The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 48,
   "name": "Role Based Access Control",
   "description": "Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups; changing a role assignment must change permissions. Supported levels include Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D04",
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D13",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential"
  },
  {
   "index": 49,
   "name": "OPAC Preservation",
   "description": "Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical"
  },
  {
   "index": 50,
   "name": "Record Data Specifications",
   "description": "The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks UD-1 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 51,
   "name": "Process Documentation",
   "description": "The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks UD-2 Medium Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 52,
   "name": "Online System Help",
   "description": "The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions and is accessible within the system and to screen readers.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks UD-3 High Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 53,
   "name": "Error Feedback",
   "description": "The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D10 marks UD-4 Medium Priority"
  },
  {
   "index": 54,
   "name": "Staff Authentication",
   "description": "The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D13",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 55,
   "name": "Report Template Controls",
   "description": "Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 56,
   "name": "Report Permission Administration",
   "description": "The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 57,
   "name": "Multi Record Query Designer",
   "description": "The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, Boolean operators, and administrator control over tables, fields, and tool access.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 58,
   "name": "Executive Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 59,
   "name": "Privacy Preserving Archives",
   "description": "The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements"
  },
  {
   "index": 60,
   "name": "Periodic Management Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide periodic reports for records with holds, items not checked out for a configurable period, item-level holds, invalid item types, in-transit items with holds, overdue transit, last copies, long call numbers, missing items, bibliographic records without items, and patrons with invalid home branches.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D05",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 61,
   "name": "Query Criteria Display",
   "description": "Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 62,
   "name": "Report Queue Monitoring",
   "description": "Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D18",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 63,
   "name": "Patron Behavior Statistics",
   "description": "The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 64,
   "name": "Anonymized Demographic Statistics",
   "description": "The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 65,
   "name": "Uncataloged Material Control",
   "description": "The system must track uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books before catalog records exist, support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify usage, and include their transactions in circulation statistics and reports.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 66,
   "name": "Collection And Capacity Analysis",
   "description": "The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections, material use, branch capacity, patron demographics, staff workflow, financial transactions, and cross-branch performance for planning, evaluation, and oversight.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D02",
    "D03",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15",
    "D17",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 67,
   "name": "Consortium Statistical Reports",
   "description": "The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D17"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 68,
   "name": "Data Quality Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 69,
   "name": "Vendor Data Integration",
   "description": "Management processes must exchange standard-format data with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, and must continue to function when vendor data is unavailable at a branch.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 70,
   "name": "Acquisitions Cataloging Integration",
   "description": "Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 71,
   "name": "OPAC Data Querying",
   "description": "Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 72,
   "name": "Report Types",
   "description": "The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 73,
   "name": "Scheduled Canned Reports",
   "description": "Users must be able to run product-delivered canned reports using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data, select multiple canned reports, and combine their output in one document.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 74,
   "name": "On Demand Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 75,
   "name": "Report Scheduling",
   "description": "Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 76,
   "name": "Report Export Formats",
   "description": "Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 77,
   "name": "Email Report Delivery",
   "description": "The system must deliver reports by email, allow users to enter recipients, and provide an address book for regularly used addresses.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 78,
   "name": "Comparative Report Output",
   "description": "Reports must support comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage differences, and the corresponding month of the previous year.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 79,
   "name": "Report Queue Prioritization",
   "description": "Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D12 describes report prioritization as crucial"
  },
  {
   "index": 80,
   "name": "Item Use Metrics",
   "description": "Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D03",
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 81,
   "name": "File Based Filtering",
   "description": "Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report filters.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 82,
   "name": "Notice Reports",
   "description": "The system must report pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 83,
   "name": "Pivot Table Output",
   "description": "The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 84,
   "name": "Report Accuracy",
   "description": "Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 85,
   "name": "Report Cancellation",
   "description": "Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 86,
   "name": "Null Field Inclusion",
   "description": "Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 87,
   "name": "Real Time Reporting",
   "description": "The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 88,
   "name": "Historical Reporting",
   "description": "The system must provide historical reporting through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D01",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 89,
   "name": "Survey Name Filtering",
   "description": "Users must be able to select a survey by name for filtering, with the system resolving the name to its survey identifier internally.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D19"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 90,
   "name": "MARC Row Consolidation",
   "description": "Reports must retrieve specified MARC fields and display them on one row even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 91,
   "name": "Workstation Transaction Reports",
   "description": "The system must report transactions for a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D20"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 92,
   "name": "Collection Value Reports",
   "description": "The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 93,
   "name": "Financial Compliance",
   "description": "Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 94,
   "name": "Financial Record Association",
   "description": "The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 95,
   "name": "High Balance Queries",
   "description": "Staff must be able to query patron accounts with balances above a user-specified dollar amount.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 96,
   "name": "Financial Data Updates",
   "description": "Authorized staff must be able to update financial information easily, and a payment made at a staff desk must be reflected immediately.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 97,
   "name": "Financial Reports",
   "description": "The system must report patron balances by patron, home branch, and library system; fines and charges by period and charge type; waived fines by period and branch; and payments by period, collecting branch, payment channel, and payment type.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D14"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": null
  },
  {
   "index": 98,
   "name": "Payment Audit Ledger",
   "description": "The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11"
   ],
   "source_priority_note": "D11 marks this requirement CRITICAL"
  },

Queue visibility helps users understand delays and failures, and five sources request this useful operational transparency.
Renewal and return-speed statistics help assess patron behavior and material use, but are analytical additions to core reporting.
Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, a useful cross-source analysis capability.

Notice counts answer a narrow circulation question and are requested by one source, so they can follow broader report capabilities.
Pivot-table output helps users summarize and explore results, and multiple sources request it as a useful analysis format.

Selecting surveys by name is a usability improvement for a narrow filtering task that can be handled through identifiers.
Consolidating MARC fields onto one row simplifies a specific kind of report, but is not needed for general bibliographic reporting.
Workstation and staff transaction reports support operational review, but cover a narrower audit use than general circulation reporting.

Bill and debt reports support financial follow-up, but are a specific part of the wider financial reporting capability.

Director-level financial reports support leadership oversight, though they serve a specific audience and reporting domain.

inputs.name: Material Volume Reporting
inputs.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library system or branch at the current or a historical date, including total items, new acquisitions, checked-in items, checked-out items, holds, adult fiction, and board books; checked-out items must count toward the total, and category groupings must be configurable by library system, such as fiction/non-fiction or format.
inputs.priority_justification: Material-volume reporting is identified as a key requirement in D01 and is supported by three sources, making it a central management-reporting capability.
inputs.source_priority_note: D01 identifies the Material Volume Report as a key requirement

inputs.name: Acquisition Volume Trends
inputs.description: The system must use item acquisition dates to report material added during selectable periods, including the preceding 30, 60, or 90 days.
inputs.priority_justification: Acquisition trends help staff monitor collection growth, but reporting acquisitions over selectable periods can be added after core reporting is available.

inputs.name: Branch Capacity Overview
inputs.description: The system must provide authorized branch managers with an all-branch capacity view, allow drilldown to an individual branch, show capacity trends such as growth or shrinkage, and support comparison for up to 286 branches.
inputs.priority_justification: An all-branch view helps managers compare capacity across the consortium, though the system can operate without this specialized overview.

inputs.name: Branch Capacity Navigation
inputs.description: The capacity view must allow users to filter and sort branches by region, library type, and current load.
inputs.priority_justification: Filtering and sorting make the capacity view more convenient to navigate, but they are refinements to a single report.

inputs.name: Capacity Data Export
inputs.description: The system must allow users to export capacity-view data in CSV format.
inputs.priority_justification: CSV export is a useful convenience for further analysis, but the capacity data remains usable within the system without it.

inputs.name: Shelf Space Analysis
inputs.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space, with views by branch and for the library system, selectable date ranges such as Q1 or Q2, collection percentages based on item counts, circulation percentages based on checkouts, and shelf-space estimates based on item dimensions or item count when dimensions are unavailable.
inputs.priority_justification: This multi-source analysis helps managers relate collection allocation to use and shelf space, though it is a specialized planning capability.

inputs.name: Shelf Space Comparisons
inputs.description: The system must show shelf-space analysis for branches side by side, including genre-and-format percentages for circulations, collection holdings, and shelf space, so users can identify differences and outliers.
inputs.priority_justification: Side-by-side comparisons make it easier to spot branch outliers, but depend on the broader shelf-space analysis being available first.

inputs.name: Batch Item Transfers
inputs.description: Authorized staff must be able to transfer selected batches of items between branches and other destinations, including mobile libraries, outreach programs, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, by changing item locations or generating pull lists; the operation must process approximately 9.6 million items without excessive database locking.
inputs.priority_justification: Batch transfers support recurring collection movement across branches and destinations, but this operational workflow is not required for the reporting system's core purpose.

inputs.name: Transfer Candidate Queries
inputs.description: Staff must be able to query for candidate items for transfer using criteria such as genre, collection area, and circulation inactivity, including items that have not circulated for six months.
inputs.priority_justification: Transfer-candidate queries help staff identify suitable items using several sources' requested criteria, while transfers can still be initiated through other selection methods.

inputs.name: Saved Transfer Queries
inputs.description: Staff must be able to save transfer-candidate queries for repeated use, including monthly reuse, and make saved queries available for reuse or sharing.
inputs.priority_justification: Saved queries reduce effort for repeated transfers, but are a convenience layered on top of candidate querying.

inputs.name: Transfer Item Selection
inputs.description: Staff must be able to manually select individual titles or items from transfer-query results before executing a transfer, such as selecting 25 items from 100 candidates.
inputs.priority_justification: Manual selection lets staff limit transfers to appropriate results and avoid moving every candidate, improving control of the transfer workflow.

inputs.name: Transfer Location Updates
inputs.description: The system must update the location field and associated item records for selected items moved to a new location.
inputs.priority_justification: Updating item locations is needed to keep records accurate when a transfer occurs, although it supports a secondary operational workflow.

inputs.name: Transfer Pull Lists
inputs.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer.
inputs.priority_justification: Printable pull lists assist staff carrying out transfers, but are an alternative operational aid rather than a core system capability.

inputs.name: Transfer Reversion
inputs.description: The system must return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or configured event, including a status change to sold or returned or checkout at the destination.
inputs.priority_justification: Configured reversion helps return items after temporary placements or specified events, but transfers can function without automated returns.

inputs.name: Transfer Audit History
inputs.description: The system must record transfer history for each item, including enough history to determine patterns such as five transfers within one year.
inputs.priority_justification: Transfer history can reveal movement patterns, but the request appears in one source and is not needed to execute or track a transfer.

inputs.name: Transfer Confirmation Preview
inputs.description: Before execution, the system must show a transfer preview containing the item count and source and destination locations and require staff confirmation.
inputs.priority_justification: A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfers by showing the affected count and locations before execution.

inputs.name: Transfer Undo
inputs.description: Staff must be able to undo an erroneous transfer after it has been initiated or completed.
inputs.priority_justification: Undo helps recover from staff mistakes, but is a single-source safeguard that can be deferred in favor of prevention and auditability.

inputs.name: Transfer Role Permissions
inputs.description: The system must restrict transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.
inputs.priority_justification: Restricting transfers to authorized roles protects a consequential operation, and the broader role-based access capability is addressed separately.

inputs.name: Transit Label Generation
inputs.description: The system must generate printable barcode transit labels for transferred items.
inputs.priority_justification: Printable barcode labels can aid physical transit handling, but they are a convenience for one part of the transfer process.

inputs.name: Transfer Delay Alerts
inputs.description: The system must notify designated staff when a transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.
inputs.priority_justification: Delay alerts can improve follow-up on individual transfers, but notifications are not required to perform or report transfers.

inputs.name: Missing Damaged Reports
inputs.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.
inputs.priority_justification: D05 calls the per-branch report crucial for accountability, and four additional sources request missing or damaged item reporting.
inputs.source_priority_note: D05 calls the per-branch missing/damaged report crucial for accountability

inputs.name: Overdue Transit Report
inputs.description: The system must provide one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.
inputs.priority_justification: Combining overdue inbound and outbound transit records helps branches resolve delayed items, but it is one specialized operational report.

inputs.name: Purge Candidate Identification
inputs.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.
inputs.priority_justification: Customizable purge criteria help staff identify stale or unsuitable records consistently, though identification can be delivered after core reporting.

inputs.name: Batch Status Conversion
inputs.description: The system must provide a report or workflow for converting many selected items from one status to another in one batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.
inputs.priority_justification: Batch status conversion saves staff effort when handling many selected records, but it is a specialized cleanup workflow.

inputs.name: Last Copy Reporting
inputs.description: The system must report items that are the only copy within a selected branch, library system, consortium, bibliographic work, or collection grouping, including deleted last copies where applicable, so catalogers can update WorldCat and avoid inappropriate deletion.
inputs.priority_justification: D06 and D15 mark last-copy reporting critical, and four sources connect it to catalog maintenance and avoiding inappropriate deletion.
inputs.source_priority_note: D06 marks this requirement critical; D15 marks the last copy report as critical

inputs.name: Orphan Record Deletion
inputs.description: The system must provide a quick method to delete volume entries with their associated copy entries and records with no attached items.
inputs.priority_justification: Quick deletion of orphaned entries streamlines cleanup, but the request is a specialized utility appearing in three sources.

inputs.name: Protected Purge Reports
inputs.description: Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.
inputs.priority_justification: Read-only candidate reports prevent an inspection step from altering records, providing a valuable safeguard for purge work.

inputs.name: Confirmed Purge Deletion
