inputs.description: The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.
inputs.priority_justification: A separate confirmation helps prevent unintended destructive purges, although deletion itself is a specialized workflow.

inputs.name: Purge Audit Trail
inputs.description: The system must record who purged each record and when.
inputs.priority_justification: Recording who purged a record and when supports accountability, but this audit detail is requested by one source.

inputs.name: Deletion Audit Logging
inputs.description: The system must record completed and denied deletion attempts, including record type, record ID, timestamp, user, user branch, library system, and, where required, deletion reason; deletion data must support counts and queries by branch, system, date range, user, record type, and highest-volume users.
inputs.priority_justification: Detailed deletion logs support accountability and investigation across several organizational dimensions, but deletion auditing is not the system's primary workflow.

inputs.name: Patron Report Filtering
inputs.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.
inputs.priority_justification: D08 calls these reports essential, and demographic and circulation filtering is a central way staff answer patron-service and planning questions.

inputs.name: Configurable Age Ranges
inputs.description: Users must be able to configure age ranges separately for each patron report, including ranges such as 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 or 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.
inputs.priority_justification: Per-report age-range configuration accommodates differing analysis needs, but the core patron reports can work with standard age groupings.

inputs.name: Null Demographic Inclusion
inputs.description: Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.
inputs.priority_justification: Including blank demographics avoids silently skewing patron results, a concern raised in two sources.

inputs.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
inputs.description: The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.
inputs.priority_justification: Identifying inactive patrons across circulation and electronic activity supports outreach and account management, but is one specialized report.

inputs.name: Inactive Report Scope
inputs.description: The inactive patron report must list or group results by configurable organizational scopes, including library system, home branch, and county, so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.
inputs.priority_justification: Organizational grouping helps route inactive-patron work to the right staff, but is a refinement to the inactive-patron report.

inputs.name: Inactive Patron Outreach
inputs.description: The inactive patron report must include each patron's current mailing address and support CSV export for upload to an outreach system.
inputs.priority_justification: Address and CSV support make outreach easier, but this workflow is requested by one source and is not needed to identify inactive patrons.

inputs.name: Inactive Patron Exceptions
inputs.description: The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.
inputs.priority_justification: Separating fines and excluding sensitive or opted-out groups helps staff use outreach results appropriately, though it extends one report.

inputs.name: Scalable Inactive Reporting
inputs.description: For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.
inputs.priority_justification: Background execution and caching help inactive reports remain usable at the stated patron scale, but are targeted optimizations for one report.

inputs.name: Consortium Scale
inputs.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-1 High Priority, and consortium-scale support is necessary for the system to serve its stated 286-branch environment.

inputs.name: Open-Hours Performance
inputs.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources request safe operation during open or peak hours, and contention that disrupts circulation or OPAC access would impair the system's core use.

inputs.name: Server Platform Support
inputs.description: The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-2 High Priority, specifying the server platforms the product must support in the target environment.

inputs.name: Client And Browser Access
inputs.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority and D18 calls browser/client access critical, so staff access to the system depends on this capability.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical

inputs.name: Assistive Technology Access
inputs.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
inputs.priority_justification: D16 and D18 identify Section 508 accessibility as a legal requirement and mandatory, making assistive-technology access a compliance obligation.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

inputs.name: Relational Database Support
inputs.description: The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-1 High Priority, and the requested relational access underpins the system's complex cross-record reporting.

inputs.name: Standards Compliant HTML
inputs.description: Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-2 High Priority, establishing standards-compliant HTML as a specified product constraint.

inputs.name: Environment Separation
inputs.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks environment separation Medium Priority, and safe training and development spaces are useful without being prerequisites for live reporting.

inputs.name: Configuration Migration
inputs.description: The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.
inputs.priority_justification: Migrating templates, permissions, and queries reduces configuration rework across environments, but the environments can function without automated migration.

inputs.name: Role Based Access Control
inputs.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups; changing a role assignment must change permissions. Supported levels include Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority, and seven sources call for role and group controls governing access to reports and transfers.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

inputs.name: OPAC Preservation
inputs.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority, and management reporting that degrades patron access would compromise the underlying library service.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

inputs.name: Record Data Specifications
inputs.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-1 High Priority, and accurate data specifications support the cross-record reporting the product must deliver.

inputs.name: Process Documentation
inputs.description: The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks process documentation Medium Priority, and it helps administrators understand imports, validation, and reporting without blocking system operation.

inputs.name: Online System Help
inputs.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions and is accessible within the system and to screen readers.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-3 High Priority, and accessible searchable help supports staff using the system's many reporting functions.

inputs.name: Error Feedback
inputs.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-4 Medium Priority, and detailed feedback helps administrators diagnose query problems but is not required for basic reporting.

inputs.name: Staff Authentication
inputs.description: The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.
inputs.priority_justification: Individual authentication preserves accountability for staff activity, while badge login is an optional convenience rather than a core reporting feature.

inputs.name: Report Template Controls
inputs.description: Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.
inputs.priority_justification: Shared templates let administrators standardize reports while giving staff controlled flexibility, a useful capability requested by four sources.

inputs.name: Report Permission Administration
inputs.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.
inputs.priority_justification: Fine-grained report permissions help administrators safely share data and tools, complementing the broader access-control capability.

inputs.name: Multi Record Query Designer
inputs.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, Boolean operators, and administrator control over tables, fields, and tool access.
inputs.priority_justification: Four sources request a cross-record query designer, which lets staff produce management questions beyond the fixed report set.

inputs.name: Executive Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.
inputs.priority_justification: Executive and board reports support oversight and required statistical submissions, but they are a distinct audience-specific report collection.

inputs.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
inputs.description: The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.
inputs.priority_justification: D12 identifies state-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements, requiring archival statistics without retained identifying data.
inputs.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

inputs.name: Periodic Management Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide periodic reports for records with holds, items not checked out for a configurable period, item-level holds, invalid item types, in-transit items with holds, overdue transit, last copies, long call numbers, missing items, bibliographic records without items, and patrons with invalid home branches.
inputs.priority_justification: These recurring reports cover a broad set of maintenance needs across four sources, but each remains a specific management report.

inputs.name: Query Criteria Display
inputs.description: Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.
inputs.priority_justification: Showing query selections and date criteria makes results easier to interpret and reproduce, though it does not produce the underlying report data.

inputs.name: Report Queue Monitoring
inputs.description: Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.
inputs.priority_justification: Queue visibility helps users understand delays and failures, and five sources request this useful operational transparency.

inputs.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
inputs.description: The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.
inputs.priority_justification: Renewal and return-speed statistics help assess patron behavior and material use, but are analytical additions to core reporting.

inputs.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
inputs.description: The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.
inputs.priority_justification: Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, a useful cross-source analysis capability.

inputs.name: Uncataloged Material Control
inputs.description: The system must track uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books before catalog records exist, support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify usage, and include their transactions in circulation statistics and reports.
inputs.priority_justification: Tracking uncataloged items ensures their distribution and use appear in operational statistics, though it addresses a particular material workflow.

inputs.name: Collection And Capacity Analysis
inputs.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections, material use, branch capacity, patron demographics, staff workflow, financial transactions, and cross-branch performance for planning, evaluation, and oversight.
inputs.priority_justification: Seven sources describe analysis across collections, capacity, patron demographics, finances, and operations as the system's broad management purpose.

inputs.name: Consortium Statistical Reports
inputs.description: The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.
inputs.priority_justification: Consortium-wide statistical reports let the global administrator evaluate network performance, but are a specific reporting scope.

inputs.name: Data Quality Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.
inputs.priority_justification: Data-quality reports help staff find records needing correction, and four sources request such operational oversight.

inputs.name: Vendor Data Integration
inputs.description: Management processes must exchange standard-format data with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, and must continue to function when vendor data is unavailable at a branch.
inputs.priority_justification: Standard vendor-data exchange supports acquisitions and related management processes, but the reporting system can deliver value without automating every exchange.

inputs.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
inputs.description: Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.
inputs.priority_justification: Using the enterprise acquisitions and cataloging data avoids duplicating those functions, while those workflows remain outside this system's scope.

inputs.name: OPAC Data Querying
inputs.description: Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.
inputs.priority_justification: Querying OPAC-created holds and circulation makes patron-interface activity available to management reports without altering operational records.

inputs.name: Report Types
inputs.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.
inputs.priority_justification: Canned, on-demand, and open-template reporting provide the basic range of ways staff must obtain management information.

inputs.name: Scheduled Canned Reports
inputs.description: Users must be able to run product-delivered canned reports using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data, select multiple canned reports, and combine their output in one document.
inputs.priority_justification: Combining scheduled canned reports into one document saves effort, but is a convenience layered on top of report generation.

inputs.name: On Demand Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities.
inputs.priority_justification: Preselected on-demand reports support maintenance and collection development, though they are one delivery mode among several.

inputs.name: Report Scheduling
inputs.description: Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.
inputs.priority_justification: Scheduling recurring reports reduces repeated staff work and is requested by three sources, but reports can also be run manually.

inputs.name: Report Export Formats
inputs.description: Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.
inputs.priority_justification: Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV output lets staff use results in common tools, but the reports remain usable in the system without each format.

inputs.name: Email Report Delivery
inputs.description: The system must deliver reports by email, allow users to enter recipients, and provide an address book for regularly used addresses.
inputs.priority_justification: Email delivery and an address book simplify distribution, but are conveniences rather than prerequisites for producing reports.

inputs.name: Comparative Report Output
inputs.description: Reports must support comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage differences, and the corresponding month of the previous year.
inputs.priority_justification: Comparative columns add context to selected reports, but the request appears in one source and is a report-format enhancement.

inputs.name: Report Queue Prioritization
inputs.description: Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.
inputs.priority_justification: D12 describes prioritization as crucial, and controlling queue order can help time-sensitive reports finish ahead of resource-heavy work.
inputs.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial

inputs.name: Item Use Metrics
inputs.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.
inputs.priority_justification: Six sources request item-use counts across time periods and usage types, making circulation and collection-use measurement a central reporting need.

inputs.name: File Based Filtering
inputs.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report filters.
inputs.priority_justification: Uploading filter values can simplify large selection tasks, but is a specialized input method requested by two sources.

inputs.name: Notice Reports
inputs.description: The system must report pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.
inputs.priority_justification: Notice counts answer a narrow circulation question and are requested by one source, so they can follow broader report capabilities.

inputs.name: Pivot Table Output
inputs.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.
inputs.priority_justification: Pivot-table output helps users summarize and explore results, and multiple sources request it as a useful analysis format.

inputs.name: Report Accuracy
inputs.description: Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.
inputs.priority_justification: Inaccurate or unreliable reports undermine the system's central purpose of supporting management decisions.

inputs.name: Report Cancellation
inputs.description: Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.
inputs.priority_justification: Cancelling queued or running reports helps reclaim resources and correct mistaken submissions, with four sources requesting the control.

inputs.name: Null Field Inclusion
inputs.description: Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.
inputs.priority_justification: Including null and blank fields prevents records from disappearing from results, a data-completeness concern raised by five sources.

inputs.name: Real Time Reporting
inputs.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.
inputs.priority_justification: Current-data reporting helps staff see recent activity, but some reporting needs can be met using scheduled or historical data.

inputs.name: Historical Reporting
inputs.description: The system must provide historical reporting through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources request historical views, which let managers compare past conditions rather than relying only on current records.

inputs.name: Survey Name Filtering
inputs.description: Users must be able to select a survey by name for filtering, with the system resolving the name to its survey identifier internally.
inputs.priority_justification: Selecting surveys by name is a usability improvement for a narrow filtering task that can be handled through identifiers.

inputs.name: MARC Row Consolidation
inputs.description: Reports must retrieve specified MARC fields and display them on one row even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.
inputs.priority_justification: Consolidating MARC fields onto one row simplifies a specific kind of report, but is not needed for general bibliographic reporting.

inputs.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
inputs.description: The system must report transactions for a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.
inputs.priority_justification: Workstation and staff transaction reports support operational review, but cover a narrower audit use than general circulation reporting.

inputs.name: Collection Value Reports
inputs.description: The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.
inputs.priority_justification: Collection-value reporting supports budgeting and collection evaluation, though value analysis is one specialized management need.

inputs.name: Financial Compliance
inputs.description: Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
inputs.priority_justification: Financial reports and archiving must meet the specified public-sector accounting and audit requirements for the system to serve its users.

inputs.name: Financial Record Association
inputs.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.
inputs.priority_justification: Associating financial events with patron and item records enables useful reconciliation and joins, but is a specialized data capability.

inputs.name: High Balance Queries
inputs.description: Staff must be able to query patron accounts with balances above a user-specified dollar amount.
inputs.priority_justification: High-balance queries help staff find accounts meeting a chosen threshold, but are a narrow financial-reporting convenience.

inputs.name: Financial Data Updates
inputs.description: Authorized staff must be able to update financial information easily, and a payment made at a staff desk must be reflected immediately.
inputs.priority_justification: Immediate reflection of desk payments keeps financial information current, though financial updates are a secondary system workflow.

inputs.name: Financial Reports
inputs.description: The system must report patron balances by patron, home branch, and library system; fines and charges by period and charge type; waived fines by period and branch; and payments by period, collecting branch, payment channel, and payment type.
inputs.priority_justification: These reports support financial oversight across patrons, branches, periods, and payment types, but serve a defined reporting domain.

inputs.name: Payment Audit Ledger
inputs.description: The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.
inputs.priority_justification: D11 marks the payment ledger CRITICAL, and tracing applied payments is needed to reconcile patron financial records.

inputs.name: Circulation Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-ins, checkouts, overdue items and patron contact information, circulation modifiers, categories, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home branch, age, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, and total circulation by type.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources request a broad circulation report suite, covering usage measures central to library management and planning.

inputs.name: Item Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, created within a date range, missing, overdue, in transit, claimed returned, selected by use count, fines-stopped reason, weeding data, collection age, collection value, last-copy status, and batch status conversion.
inputs.priority_justification: Seven sources request item reports spanning collection status, maintenance, use, value, and last-copy needs, making this a major reporting area.

inputs.name: Bibliographic Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide bibliographic reports for record counts, edited records, records added by user and branch, records without attached volumes or items, and records missing specified MARC fields.
inputs.priority_justification: Bibliographic reports help staff review records and identify missing data, but are one component of the wider management-reporting suite.

inputs.name: Patron Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide patron reports for counts, additions by month, demographic categories, survey answers, expiration date, barred and inactive status, notes, and staff-account password-change and expiration dates, including counts by age, county, city, ZIP code, and home branch.
inputs.priority_justification: Four sources request patron reporting across counts, demographics, activity, and account status, a broad management and planning need.

inputs.name: Hold Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide hold reports for purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans, unfilled holds, annual totals, and stale holds remaining beyond the permitted pickup period.
inputs.priority_justification: Hold reports help branches monitor requests and identify stale or unfilled holds, but are a defined circulation subdomain.

inputs.name: In House Use Reports
inputs.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use by month and cataloged in-house use.
inputs.priority_justification: In-house-use reporting measures a narrow category of activity and is requested by one source.

inputs.name: Transit Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must report items in transit to a destination branch and items in transit by sending branch.
inputs.priority_justification: D18 describes in-transit reports as critical for delivery coordination, and four sources request transit visibility.
inputs.source_priority_note: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination

inputs.name: Bills Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide reports for current patron bills, detailed payments, forgive/work/goods payments, voids, and aged debt with detailed aging periods.
inputs.priority_justification: Bill and debt reports support financial follow-up, but are a specific part of the wider financial reporting capability.

inputs.name: Activity Cross Tabulation
inputs.description: Activity reports must show checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, cross-tabulated by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.
inputs.priority_justification: Cross-tabulation supports analysis of activity across branches, hours, and patron groups, but is a specialized output of reporting.

inputs.name: Transaction Grouping
inputs.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days, preserve monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely, and group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, system, transaction type, and selected dimensions.
inputs.priority_justification: Detailed transaction retention and aggregation enable trend analysis, though these are supporting capabilities for specific statistical reports.

inputs.name: Checkin Method Counts
inputs.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, staff or user processing, and self-service.
inputs.priority_justification: Counts by check-in method help evaluate service channels, but the request is a narrow metric from two sources.

inputs.name: Checkout Type Counts
inputs.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.
inputs.priority_justification: Checkout and renewal counts by method provide operational detail, but are a specific breakdown rather than a broad reporting capability.

inputs.name: Hold Placement Counts
inputs.description: The system must count hold requests and classify them by placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.
inputs.priority_justification: Classifying holds by placement method offers a narrow view of patron behavior and can be deferred behind broader activity reports.

inputs.name: Transaction Summary Reports
inputs.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts by patron, branch, selected branch groups, library system, and county, including checkout and hold subtotals and hold states such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.
inputs.priority_justification: Summaries by branch and patron grouping help managers compare checkouts and holds, but are a specific set of transaction views.

inputs.name: Accounting Data Retention
inputs.description: The system must archive financial data according to state and local requirements and enforce applicable retention policies, including seven years of audit data where required.
inputs.priority_justification: Applicable financial retention rules, including required audit-data periods, must be enforced to support accountable records management.

inputs.name: Snapshot Bills Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide bills reports showing bill information as it existed at a past point in time.
inputs.priority_justification: Past-state bill reports provide useful historical context, but are a specialized capability requested by two sources.

inputs.name: Separate Item Dates
inputs.description: Item reports must expose last-edit date, last-circulation date, and check-in date and time as separate fields; last-edit date changes only when the item is edited, and renewal timestamps must not be treated as check-ins or edits.
inputs.priority_justification: Separating edit, circulation, and check-in dates prevents staff from misinterpreting item history, and three sources request the distinctions.

inputs.name: Report Quick Access
inputs.description: The reporting interface must provide quick access to canned reports and templates, with hover or popup descriptions for report titles and templates.
inputs.priority_justification: Quick access and hover descriptions make reports easier to find, but are interface refinements rather than core reporting functions.

inputs.name: Reporting Database Isolation
inputs.description: The system must provide a separate reporting database or replica when needed to isolate reporting workloads from the production database.
inputs.priority_justification: A separate reporting database can protect production performance, complementing the broader open-hours and workload-isolation requirements.

inputs.name: Background Report Processing
inputs.description: Long-running reports must execute in the background or through a queue without occupying the user interface.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources request background processing, which lets long reports run without occupying staff interfaces or disrupting other work.

inputs.name: Report Environment Help
inputs.description: The reporting system must provide integrated online help for its reporting interface.
inputs.priority_justification: Integrated reporting help provides convenience for users, but broader online system help is addressed by a separate requirement.

inputs.name: Vendor And Library Integration
inputs.description: The system must provide a centralized service accepting input from and serving multiple branches as a single reporting source of truth.
inputs.priority_justification: A centralized source of truth across branches supports consistent consortium-wide reporting, as requested by three sources.

inputs.name: Library Report Templates
inputs.description: The product must provide report templates needed by all consortium member branches for management reporting.
inputs.priority_justification: Shared templates give member branches a common starting point for management reports, but remain one way to meet reporting needs.

inputs.name: Director Financial Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information.
inputs.priority_justification: Director-level financial reports support leadership oversight, though they serve a specific audience and reporting domain.

inputs.name: Inventory Capacity Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide inventory and capacity reports for staff monitoring collections and operational capacity.
inputs.priority_justification: Six sources request inventory and capacity reporting, enabling staff to monitor collections and operational capacity across branches.

inputs.name: Management Reporting Scope
inputs.description: The reporting functionality must support management planning, evaluation, and oversight rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled by the OPAC and circulation client.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources define management planning, evaluation, and oversight as the reporting system's scope, distinguishing it from patron-facing operations.

inputs.name: Report Data Requirements
inputs.description: The system must provide predefined reports and templates covering the management reporting needs of consortium branches.
inputs.priority_justification: Predefined reports and templates cover the management questions branches need to answer, providing a core route to useful results.

inputs.name: Save Reusable Queries
inputs.description: The system must allow staff to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting activities.
inputs.priority_justification: Reusable queries reduce repeated setup effort across several reporting activities, but reports can still be produced without saving them.

inputs.name: Select Query Results Manually
inputs.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative actions.
inputs.priority_justification: Manual result selection gives staff control over records chosen for administrative actions, complementing the transfer workflow.

outputs.name: Historical Reporting
outputs.description: The system must provide historical reporting through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.
outputs.priority_justification: Five sources request historical views, which let managers compare past conditions rather than relying only on current records.

outputs.name: Material Volume Reporting
outputs.description: The system must report material volume for a specified library system or branch at the current or a historical date, including total items, new acquisitions, checked-in items, checked-out items, holds, adult fiction, and board books; checked-out items must count toward the total, and category groupings must be configurable by library system, such as fiction/non-fiction or format.
outputs.priority_justification: Material-volume reporting is identified as a key requirement in D01 and is supported by three sources, making it a central management-reporting capability.
outputs.source_priority_note: D01 identifies the Material Volume Report as a key requirement

outputs.name: Collection And Capacity Analysis
outputs.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections, material use, branch capacity, patron demographics, staff workflow, financial transactions, and cross-branch performance for planning, evaluation, and oversight.
outputs.priority_justification: Seven sources describe analysis across collections, capacity, patron demographics, finances, and operations as the system's broad management purpose.

outputs.name: Consortium Scale
outputs.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-1 High Priority, and consortium-scale support is necessary for the system to serve its stated 286-branch environment.

outputs.name: Inventory Capacity Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide inventory and capacity reports for staff monitoring collections and operational capacity.
outputs.priority_justification: Six sources request inventory and capacity reporting, enabling staff to monitor collections and operational capacity across branches.

outputs.name: Item Use Metrics
outputs.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.
outputs.priority_justification: Six sources request item-use counts across time periods and usage types, making circulation and collection-use measurement a central reporting need.

outputs.name: Role Based Access Control
outputs.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups; changing a role assignment must change permissions. Supported levels include Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority, and seven sources call for role and group controls governing access to reports and transfers.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

outputs.name: Item Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must provide item reports for items added, deleted, edited, counted, created within a date range, missing, overdue, in transit, claimed returned, selected by use count, fines-stopped reason, weeding data, collection age, collection value, last-copy status, and batch status conversion.
outputs.priority_justification: Seven sources request item reports spanning collection status, maintenance, use, value, and last-copy needs, making this a major reporting area.

outputs.name: Missing Damaged Reports
outputs.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.
outputs.priority_justification: D05 calls the per-branch report crucial for accountability, and four additional sources request missing or damaged item reporting.
outputs.source_priority_note: D05 calls the per-branch missing/damaged report crucial for accountability

outputs.name: Transit Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must report items in transit to a destination branch and items in transit by sending branch.
outputs.priority_justification: D18 describes in-transit reports as critical for delivery coordination, and four sources request transit visibility.
outputs.source_priority_note: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination

outputs.name: Last Copy Reporting
outputs.description: The system must report items that are the only copy within a selected branch, library system, consortium, bibliographic work, or collection grouping, including deleted last copies where applicable, so catalogers can update WorldCat and avoid inappropriate deletion.
outputs.priority_justification: D06 and D15 mark last-copy reporting critical, and four sources connect it to catalog maintenance and avoiding inappropriate deletion.
outputs.source_priority_note: D06 marks this requirement critical; D15 marks the last copy report as critical

outputs.name: Circulation Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must provide circulation reports for check-ins, checkouts, overdue items and patron contact information, circulation modifiers, categories, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC fields, patron county, home branch, age, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, and total circulation by type.
outputs.priority_justification: Five sources request a broad circulation report suite, covering usage measures central to library management and planning.

outputs.name: Patron Report Filtering
outputs.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.
outputs.priority_justification: D08 calls these reports essential, and demographic and circulation filtering is a central way staff answer patron-service and planning questions.

outputs.name: Patron Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must provide patron reports for counts, additions by month, demographic categories, survey answers, expiration date, barred and inactive status, notes, and staff-account password-change and expiration dates, including counts by age, county, city, ZIP code, and home branch.
outputs.priority_justification: Four sources request patron reporting across counts, demographics, activity, and account status, a broad management and planning need.

outputs.name: Background Report Processing
outputs.description: Long-running reports must execute in the background or through a queue without occupying the user interface.
outputs.priority_justification: Five sources request background processing, which lets long reports run without occupying staff interfaces or disrupting other work.

outputs.name: Accounting Data Retention
outputs.description: The system must archive financial data according to state and local requirements and enforce applicable retention policies, including seven years of audit data where required.
outputs.priority_justification: Applicable financial retention rules, including required audit-data periods, must be enforced to support accountable records management.

outputs.name: Assistive Technology Access
outputs.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
outputs.priority_justification: D16 and D18 identify Section 508 accessibility as a legal requirement and mandatory, making assistive-technology access a compliance obligation.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

outputs.name: Client And Browser Access
outputs.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority and D18 calls browser/client access critical, so staff access to the system depends on this capability.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical

outputs.name: Financial Compliance
outputs.description: Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
outputs.priority_justification: Financial reports and archiving must meet the specified public-sector accounting and audit requirements for the system to serve its users.

outputs.name: Management Reporting Scope
outputs.description: The reporting functionality must support management planning, evaluation, and oversight rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled by the OPAC and circulation client.
outputs.priority_justification: Five sources define management planning, evaluation, and oversight as the reporting system's scope, distinguishing it from patron-facing operations.

outputs.name: Multi Record Query Designer
outputs.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, Boolean operators, and administrator control over tables, fields, and tool access.
outputs.priority_justification: Four sources request a cross-record query designer, which lets staff produce management questions beyond the fixed report set.

outputs.name: Online System Help
outputs.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions and is accessible within the system and to screen readers.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-3 High Priority, and accessible searchable help supports staff using the system's many reporting functions.

outputs.name: OPAC Preservation
outputs.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority, and management reporting that degrades patron access would compromise the underlying library service.
outputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

outputs.name: Open-Hours Performance
outputs.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.
outputs.priority_justification: Five sources request safe operation during open or peak hours, and contention that disrupts circulation or OPAC access would impair the system's core use.

outputs.name: Payment Audit Ledger
outputs.description: The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.
outputs.priority_justification: D11 marks the payment ledger CRITICAL, and tracing applied payments is needed to reconcile patron financial records.

outputs.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
outputs.description: The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.
outputs.priority_justification: D12 identifies state-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements, requiring archival statistics without retained identifying data.
outputs.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

outputs.name: Record Data Specifications
outputs.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-1 High Priority, and accurate data specifications support the cross-record reporting the product must deliver.

outputs.name: Relational Database Support
outputs.description: The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-1 High Priority, and the requested relational access underpins the system's complex cross-record reporting.

outputs.name: Report Accuracy
outputs.description: Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.
outputs.priority_justification: Inaccurate or unreliable reports undermine the system's central purpose of supporting management decisions.

outputs.name: Report Data Requirements
outputs.description: The system must provide predefined reports and templates covering the management reporting needs of consortium branches.
outputs.priority_justification: Predefined reports and templates cover the management questions branches need to answer, providing a core route to useful results.

outputs.name: Report Types
outputs.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.
outputs.priority_justification: Canned, on-demand, and open-template reporting provide the basic range of ways staff must obtain management information.

outputs.name: Server Platform Support
outputs.description: The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-2 High Priority, specifying the server platforms the product must support in the target environment.

outputs.name: Standards Compliant HTML
outputs.description: Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-2 High Priority, establishing standards-compliant HTML as a specified product constraint.

outputs.name: Vendor And Library Integration
outputs.description: The system must provide a centralized service accepting input from and serving multiple branches as a single reporting source of truth.
outputs.priority_justification: A centralized source of truth across branches supports consistent consortium-wide reporting, as requested by three sources.

outputs.name: Acquisition Volume Trends
outputs.description: The system must use item acquisition dates to report material added during selectable periods, including the preceding 30, 60, or 90 days.
outputs.priority_justification: Acquisition trends help staff monitor collection growth, but reporting acquisitions over selectable periods can be added after core reporting is available.

outputs.name: Branch Capacity Overview
outputs.description: The system must provide authorized branch managers with an all-branch capacity view, allow drilldown to an individual branch, show capacity trends such as growth or shrinkage, and support comparison for up to 286 branches.
outputs.priority_justification: An all-branch view helps managers compare capacity across the consortium, though the system can operate without this specialized overview.

outputs.name: Shelf Space Analysis
outputs.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space, with views by branch and for the library system, selectable date ranges such as Q1 or Q2, collection percentages based on item counts, circulation percentages based on checkouts, and shelf-space estimates based on item dimensions or item count when dimensions are unavailable.
outputs.priority_justification: This multi-source analysis helps managers relate collection allocation to use and shelf space, though it is a specialized planning capability.

outputs.name: Batch Item Transfers
outputs.description: Authorized staff must be able to transfer selected batches of items between branches and other destinations, including mobile libraries, outreach programs, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, by changing item locations or generating pull lists; the operation must process approximately 9.6 million items without excessive database locking.
outputs.priority_justification: Batch transfers support recurring collection movement across branches and destinations, but this operational workflow is not required for the reporting system's core purpose.

outputs.name: Select Query Results Manually
outputs.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative actions.
outputs.priority_justification: Manual result selection gives staff control over records chosen for administrative actions, complementing the transfer workflow.

outputs.name: Transfer Candidate Queries
outputs.description: Staff must be able to query for candidate items for transfer using criteria such as genre, collection area, and circulation inactivity, including items that have not circulated for six months.
outputs.priority_justification: Transfer-candidate queries help staff identify suitable items using several sources' requested criteria, while transfers can still be initiated through other selection methods.

outputs.name: Transfer Confirmation Preview
outputs.description: Before execution, the system must show a transfer preview containing the item count and source and destination locations and require staff confirmation.
outputs.priority_justification: A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfers by showing the affected count and locations before execution.

outputs.name: Transfer Item Selection
outputs.description: Staff must be able to manually select individual titles or items from transfer-query results before executing a transfer, such as selecting 25 items from 100 candidates.
outputs.priority_justification: Manual selection lets staff limit transfers to appropriate results and avoid moving every candidate, improving control of the transfer workflow.

outputs.name: Transfer Location Updates
outputs.description: The system must update the location field and associated item records for selected items moved to a new location.
outputs.priority_justification: Updating item locations is needed to keep records accurate when a transfer occurs, although it supports a secondary operational workflow.

outputs.name: Transfer Reversion
outputs.description: The system must return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or configured event, including a status change to sold or returned or checkout at the destination.
outputs.priority_justification: Configured reversion helps return items after temporary placements or specified events, but transfers can function without automated returns.

outputs.name: Transfer Role Permissions
outputs.description: The system must restrict transfers to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.
outputs.priority_justification: Restricting transfers to authorized roles protects a consequential operation, and the broader role-based access capability is addressed separately.

outputs.name: Overdue Transit Report
outputs.description: The system must provide one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.
outputs.priority_justification: Combining overdue inbound and outbound transit records helps branches resolve delayed items, but it is one specialized operational report.

outputs.name: Periodic Management Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide periodic reports for records with holds, items not checked out for a configurable period, item-level holds, invalid item types, in-transit items with holds, overdue transit, last copies, long call numbers, missing items, bibliographic records without items, and patrons with invalid home branches.
outputs.priority_justification: These recurring reports cover a broad set of maintenance needs across four sources, but each remains a specific management report.

outputs.name: Batch Status Conversion
outputs.description: The system must provide a report or workflow for converting many selected items from one status to another in one batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.
outputs.priority_justification: Batch status conversion saves staff effort when handling many selected records, but it is a specialized cleanup workflow.

outputs.name: Confirmed Purge Deletion
outputs.description: The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.
outputs.priority_justification: A separate confirmation helps prevent unintended destructive purges, although deletion itself is a specialized workflow.

outputs.name: Deletion Audit Logging
outputs.description: The system must record completed and denied deletion attempts, including record type, record ID, timestamp, user, user branch, library system, and, where required, deletion reason; deletion data must support counts and queries by branch, system, date range, user, record type, and highest-volume users.
outputs.priority_justification: Detailed deletion logs support accountability and investigation across several organizational dimensions, but deletion auditing is not the system's primary workflow.

outputs.name: Protected Purge Reports
outputs.description: Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.
outputs.priority_justification: Read-only candidate reports prevent an inspection step from altering records, providing a valuable safeguard for purge work.

outputs.name: Purge Audit Trail
outputs.description: The system must record who purged each record and when.
outputs.priority_justification: Recording who purged a record and when supports accountability, but this audit detail is requested by one source.

outputs.name: Purge Candidate Identification
outputs.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.
outputs.priority_justification: Customizable purge criteria help staff identify stale or unsuitable records consistently, though identification can be delivered after core reporting.

outputs.name: Activity Cross Tabulation
outputs.description: Activity reports must show checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, cross-tabulated by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.
outputs.priority_justification: Cross-tabulation supports analysis of activity across branches, hours, and patron groups, but is a specialized output of reporting.

outputs.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
outputs.description: The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.
outputs.priority_justification: Identifying inactive patrons across circulation and electronic activity supports outreach and account management, but is one specialized report.

outputs.name: Null Demographic Inclusion
outputs.description: Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.
outputs.priority_justification: Including blank demographics avoids silently skewing patron results, a concern raised in two sources.

outputs.name: Null Field Inclusion
outputs.description: Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.
outputs.priority_justification: Including null and blank fields prevents records from disappearing from results, a data-completeness concern raised by five sources.

outputs.name: Inactive Patron Exceptions
outputs.description: The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.
outputs.priority_justification: Separating fines and excluding sensitive or opted-out groups helps staff use outreach results appropriately, though it extends one report.

outputs.name: Report Export Formats
outputs.description: Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.
outputs.priority_justification: Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV output lets staff use results in common tools, but the reports remain usable in the system without each format.

outputs.name: Scalable Inactive Reporting
outputs.description: For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.
outputs.priority_justification: Background execution and caching help inactive reports remain usable at the stated patron scale, but are targeted optimizations for one report.

outputs.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
outputs.description: Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.
outputs.priority_justification: Using the enterprise acquisitions and cataloging data avoids duplicating those functions, while those workflows remain outside this system's scope.

outputs.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
outputs.description: The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.
outputs.priority_justification: Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, a useful cross-source analysis capability.

outputs.name: Bibliographic Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide bibliographic reports for record counts, edited records, records added by user and branch, records without attached volumes or items, and records missing specified MARC fields.
outputs.priority_justification: Bibliographic reports help staff review records and identify missing data, but are one component of the wider management-reporting suite.

outputs.name: Bills Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must provide reports for current patron bills, detailed payments, forgive/work/goods payments, voids, and aged debt with detailed aging periods.
outputs.priority_justification: Bill and debt reports support financial follow-up, but are a specific part of the wider financial reporting capability.

outputs.name: Collection Value Reports
outputs.description: The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.
outputs.priority_justification: Collection-value reporting supports budgeting and collection evaluation, though value analysis is one specialized management need.

outputs.name: Configuration Migration
outputs.description: The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.
outputs.priority_justification: Migrating templates, permissions, and queries reduces configuration rework across environments, but the environments can function without automated migration.

outputs.name: Consortium Statistical Reports
outputs.description: The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.
outputs.priority_justification: Consortium-wide statistical reports let the global administrator evaluate network performance, but are a specific reporting scope.

outputs.name: Data Quality Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.
outputs.priority_justification: Data-quality reports help staff find records needing correction, and four sources request such operational oversight.

outputs.name: Director Financial Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information.
outputs.priority_justification: Director-level financial reports support leadership oversight, though they serve a specific audience and reporting domain.

outputs.name: Environment Separation
outputs.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks environment separation Medium Priority, and safe training and development spaces are useful without being prerequisites for live reporting.

outputs.name: Error Feedback
outputs.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-4 Medium Priority, and detailed feedback helps administrators diagnose query problems but is not required for basic reporting.

outputs.name: Executive Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.
outputs.priority_justification: Executive and board reports support oversight and required statistical submissions, but they are a distinct audience-specific report collection.

outputs.name: Financial Data Updates
outputs.description: Authorized staff must be able to update financial information easily, and a payment made at a staff desk must be reflected immediately.
outputs.priority_justification: Immediate reflection of desk payments keeps financial information current, though financial updates are a secondary system workflow.

outputs.name: Financial Record Association
outputs.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.
outputs.priority_justification: Associating financial events with patron and item records enables useful reconciliation and joins, but is a specialized data capability.

outputs.name: Financial Reports
outputs.description: The system must report patron balances by patron, home branch, and library system; fines and charges by period and charge type; waived fines by period and branch; and payments by period, collecting branch, payment channel, and payment type.
outputs.priority_justification: These reports support financial oversight across patrons, branches, periods, and payment types, but serve a defined reporting domain.

outputs.name: Hold Report Suite
outputs.description: The system must provide hold reports for purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans, unfilled holds, annual totals, and stale holds remaining beyond the permitted pickup period.
outputs.priority_justification: Hold reports help branches monitor requests and identify stale or unfilled holds, but are a defined circulation subdomain.

outputs.name: Library Report Templates
outputs.description: The product must provide report templates needed by all consortium member branches for management reporting.
outputs.priority_justification: Shared templates give member branches a common starting point for management reports, but remain one way to meet reporting needs.

outputs.name: On Demand Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities.
outputs.priority_justification: Preselected on-demand reports support maintenance and collection development, though they are one delivery mode among several.

outputs.name: OPAC Data Querying
outputs.description: Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.
outputs.priority_justification: Querying OPAC-created holds and circulation makes patron-interface activity available to management reports without altering operational records.

outputs.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
outputs.description: The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.
outputs.priority_justification: Renewal and return-speed statistics help assess patron behavior and material use, but are analytical additions to core reporting.

outputs.name: Pivot Table Output
outputs.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.
outputs.priority_justification: Pivot-table output helps users summarize and explore results, and multiple sources request it as a useful analysis format.

outputs.name: Process Documentation
outputs.description: The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
outputs.priority_justification: D10 marks process documentation Medium Priority, and it helps administrators understand imports, validation, and reporting without blocking system operation.

outputs.name: Query Criteria Display
outputs.description: Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.
outputs.priority_justification: Showing query selections and date criteria makes results easier to interpret and reproduce, though it does not produce the underlying report data.

outputs.name: Real Time Reporting
outputs.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.
outputs.priority_justification: Current-data reporting helps staff see recent activity, but some reporting needs can be met using scheduled or historical data.

outputs.name: Report Cancellation
outputs.description: Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.
outputs.priority_justification: Cancelling queued or running reports helps reclaim resources and correct mistaken submissions, with four sources requesting the control.

outputs.name: Report Permission Administration
outputs.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.
outputs.priority_justification: Fine-grained report permissions help administrators safely share data and tools, complementing the broader access-control capability.

outputs.name: Report Queue Monitoring
outputs.description: Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.
outputs.priority_justification: Queue visibility helps users understand delays and failures, and five sources request this useful operational transparency.

outputs.name: Report Queue Prioritization
outputs.description: Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.
outputs.priority_justification: D12 describes prioritization as crucial, and controlling queue order can help time-sensitive reports finish ahead of resource-heavy work.
outputs.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial

outputs.name: Report Scheduling
outputs.description: Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.
outputs.priority_justification: Scheduling recurring reports reduces repeated staff work and is requested by three sources, but reports can also be run manually.

outputs.name: Report Template Controls
outputs.description: Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.
outputs.priority_justification: Shared templates let administrators standardize reports while giving staff controlled flexibility, a useful capability requested by four sources.

outputs.name: Save Reusable Queries
outputs.description: The system must allow staff to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting activities.
outputs.priority_justification: Reusable queries reduce repeated setup effort across several reporting activities, but reports can still be produced without saving them.

outputs.name: Staff Authentication
outputs.description: The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.
