outputs.priority_justification: Individual authentication preserves accountability for staff activity, while badge login is an optional convenience rather than a core reporting feature.

outputs.name: Transaction Grouping
outputs.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days, preserve monthly and annual aggregates indefinitely, and group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, system, transaction type, and selected dimensions.
outputs.priority_justification: Detailed transaction retention and aggregation enable trend analysis, though these are supporting capabilities for specific statistical reports.

outputs.name: Transaction Summary Reports
outputs.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts by patron, branch, selected branch groups, library system, and county, including checkout and hold subtotals and hold states such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.
outputs.priority_justification: Summaries by branch and patron grouping help managers compare checkouts and holds, but are a specific set of transaction views.

outputs.name: Uncataloged Material Control
outputs.description: The system must track uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books before catalog records exist, support rapid distribution with minimal branch labor, identify usage, and include their transactions in circulation statistics and reports.
outputs.priority_justification: Tracking uncataloged items ensures their distribution and use appear in operational statistics, though it addresses a particular material workflow.

outputs.name: Vendor Data Integration
outputs.description: Management processes must exchange standard-format data with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfers, including USMARC21 and EDIFACT, and must continue to function when vendor data is unavailable at a branch.
outputs.priority_justification: Standard vendor-data exchange supports acquisitions and related management processes, but the reporting system can deliver value without automating every exchange.

outputs.name: Workstation Transaction Reports
outputs.description: The system must report transactions for a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member.
outputs.priority_justification: Workstation and staff transaction reports support operational review, but cover a narrower audit use than general circulation reporting.

outputs.name: Reporting Database Isolation
outputs.description: The system must provide a separate reporting database or replica when needed to isolate reporting workloads from the production database.
outputs.priority_justification: A separate reporting database can protect production performance, complementing the broader open-hours and workload-isolation requirements.

outputs.name: Separate Item Dates
outputs.description: Item reports must expose last-edit date, last-circulation date, and check-in date and time as separate fields; last-edit date changes only when the item is edited, and renewal timestamps must not be treated as check-ins or edits.
outputs.priority_justification: Separating edit, circulation, and check-in dates prevents staff from misinterpreting item history, and three sources request the distinctions.

outputs.name: Branch Capacity Navigation
outputs.description: The capacity view must allow users to filter and sort branches by region, library type, and current load.
outputs.priority_justification: Filtering and sorting make the capacity view more convenient to navigate, but they are refinements to a single report.

outputs.name: Capacity Data Export
outputs.description: The system must allow users to export capacity-view data in CSV format.
outputs.priority_justification: CSV export is a useful convenience for further analysis, but the capacity data remains usable within the system without it.

outputs.name: Shelf Space Comparisons
outputs.description: The system must show shelf-space analysis for branches side by side, including genre-and-format percentages for circulations, collection holdings, and shelf space, so users can identify differences and outliers.
outputs.priority_justification: Side-by-side comparisons make it easier to spot branch outliers, but depend on the broader shelf-space analysis being available first.

outputs.name: Saved Transfer Queries
outputs.description: Staff must be able to save transfer-candidate queries for repeated use, including monthly reuse, and make saved queries available for reuse or sharing.
outputs.priority_justification: Saved queries reduce effort for repeated transfers, but are a convenience layered on top of candidate querying.

outputs.name: Transfer Audit History
outputs.description: The system must record transfer history for each item, including enough history to determine patterns such as five transfers within one year.
outputs.priority_justification: Transfer history can reveal movement patterns, but the request appears in one source and is not needed to execute or track a transfer.

outputs.name: Transfer Delay Alerts
outputs.description: The system must notify designated staff when a transfer is delayed or encounters an issue.
outputs.priority_justification: Delay alerts can improve follow-up on individual transfers, but notifications are not required to perform or report transfers.

outputs.name: Transfer Pull Lists
outputs.description: The system must generate printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer.
outputs.priority_justification: Printable pull lists assist staff carrying out transfers, but are an alternative operational aid rather than a core system capability.

outputs.name: Transfer Undo
outputs.description: Staff must be able to undo an erroneous transfer after it has been initiated or completed.
outputs.priority_justification: Undo helps recover from staff mistakes, but is a single-source safeguard that can be deferred in favor of prevention and auditability.

outputs.name: Transit Label Generation
outputs.description: The system must generate printable barcode transit labels for transferred items.
outputs.priority_justification: Printable barcode labels can aid physical transit handling, but they are a convenience for one part of the transfer process.

outputs.name: Orphan Record Deletion
outputs.description: The system must provide a quick method to delete volume entries with their associated copy entries and records with no attached items.
outputs.priority_justification: Quick deletion of orphaned entries streamlines cleanup, but the request is a specialized utility appearing in three sources.

outputs.name: Configurable Age Ranges
outputs.description: Users must be able to configure age ranges separately for each patron report, including ranges such as 0–5, 6–10, 11–15 or 0–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–24, and 25–34.
outputs.priority_justification: Per-report age-range configuration accommodates differing analysis needs, but the core patron reports can work with standard age groupings.

outputs.name: Inactive Patron Outreach
outputs.description: The inactive patron report must include each patron's current mailing address and support CSV export for upload to an outreach system.
outputs.priority_justification: Address and CSV support make outreach easier, but this workflow is requested by one source and is not needed to identify inactive patrons.

outputs.name: Inactive Report Scope
outputs.description: The inactive patron report must list or group results by configurable organizational scopes, including library system, home branch, and county, so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.
outputs.priority_justification: Organizational grouping helps route inactive-patron work to the right staff, but is a refinement to the inactive-patron report.

outputs.name: Checkin Method Counts
outputs.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, staff or user processing, and self-service.
outputs.priority_justification: Counts by check-in method help evaluate service channels, but the request is a narrow metric from two sources.

outputs.name: Checkout Type Counts
outputs.description: The system must count checkouts individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.
outputs.priority_justification: Checkout and renewal counts by method provide operational detail, but are a specific breakdown rather than a broad reporting capability.

outputs.name: Comparative Report Output
outputs.description: Reports must support comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage differences, and the corresponding month of the previous year.
outputs.priority_justification: Comparative columns add context to selected reports, but the request appears in one source and is a report-format enhancement.

outputs.name: Email Report Delivery
outputs.description: The system must deliver reports by email, allow users to enter recipients, and provide an address book for regularly used addresses.
outputs.priority_justification: Email delivery and an address book simplify distribution, but are conveniences rather than prerequisites for producing reports.

outputs.name: File Based Filtering
outputs.description: Users must be able to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report filters.
outputs.priority_justification: Uploading filter values can simplify large selection tasks, but is a specialized input method requested by two sources.

outputs.name: High Balance Queries
outputs.description: Staff must be able to query patron accounts with balances above a user-specified dollar amount.
outputs.priority_justification: High-balance queries help staff find accounts meeting a chosen threshold, but are a narrow financial-reporting convenience.

outputs.name: Hold Placement Counts
outputs.description: The system must count hold requests and classify them by placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.
outputs.priority_justification: Classifying holds by placement method offers a narrow view of patron behavior and can be deferred behind broader activity reports.

outputs.name: In House Use Reports
outputs.description: The system must report non-cataloged in-house use by month and cataloged in-house use.
outputs.priority_justification: In-house-use reporting measures a narrow category of activity and is requested by one source.

outputs.name: MARC Row Consolidation
outputs.description: Reports must retrieve specified MARC fields and display them on one row even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.
outputs.priority_justification: Consolidating MARC fields onto one row simplifies a specific kind of report, but is not needed for general bibliographic reporting.

outputs.name: Notice Reports
outputs.description: The system must report pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.
outputs.priority_justification: Notice counts answer a narrow circulation question and are requested by one source, so they can follow broader report capabilities.

outputs.name: Report Environment Help
outputs.description: The reporting system must provide integrated online help for its reporting interface.
outputs.priority_justification: Integrated reporting help provides convenience for users, but broader online system help is addressed by a separate requirement.

outputs.name: Report Quick Access
outputs.description: The reporting interface must provide quick access to canned reports and templates, with hover or popup descriptions for report titles and templates.
outputs.priority_justification: Quick access and hover descriptions make reports easier to find, but are interface refinements rather than core reporting functions.

outputs.name: Scheduled Canned Reports
outputs.description: Users must be able to run product-delivered canned reports using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data, select multiple canned reports, and combine their output in one document.
outputs.priority_justification: Combining scheduled canned reports into one document saves effort, but is a convenience layered on top of report generation.

outputs.name: Survey Name Filtering
outputs.description: Users must be able to select a survey by name for filtering, with the system resolving the name to its survey identifier internally.
outputs.priority_justification: Selecting surveys by name is a usability improvement for a narrow filtering task that can be handled through identifiers.

outputs.name: Snapshot Bills Reports
outputs.description: The system must provide bills reports showing bill information as it existed at a past point in time.
outputs.priority_justification: Past-state bill reports provide useful historical context, but are a specialized capability requested by two sources.

You are the reviewer of a requirements document. The user message is JSON with the current requirements (with ids R01...), the glossary, the blacklist of discarded requirements (context only), the review round and the maximum number of rounds.

Validate the list itself; you do not have the corpus, so do not ask for new requirements. Flag defects only, things a careful reader would call wrong, not things that are merely imperfect. Each issue lists the involved requirement ids and explains the problem concretely. Issue types:
- duplicate: two or more requirements that ask for the same capability (not one that duplicates a blacklisted item).
- conflict: two requirements that cannot both be satisfied by one system (logically incompatible). A rule interacting with another feature (for example a null-inclusion rule and a filter) is not a conflict; when in doubt, raise wording.
- wording: vocabulary inconsistent with the glossary, or a name that does not match its description.
- nonsense: an item that is not a software requirement or makes no sense.
- too_broad: one issue per requirement that clearly bundles several independently testable capabilities per the definition below. Length alone is not a reason, and a description that lists several options, filters or fields of one capability is not too_broad.
- too_narrow: a requirement that is only a detail of another (one filter option, one field, one exclusion rule of a report or utility). requirement_ids contain both the detail and its parent, and the explanation says which is which.
- priority: a priority that is implausible under the scale below or clashes with its own justification.
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Requirements tagged "[granularity settled]" next to their id were already split or folded by a resolver: raise no too_broad or too_narrow on them (the other issue types still apply).

Route:
- accept: the list is clean, the remaining concerns are matters of taste, or they are only granularity concerns on "[granularity settled]" requirements.
- targeted: there are defects worth fixing.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

Example of a statement that is too broad: "Staff can manage item transfers between branches, including selecting candidate items by circulation history and keeping an audit history of every completed transfer." This is exactly two requirements: (1) select transfer candidates by circulation history, (2) record an audit history of completed transfers.
Example of statements that are too narrow: "The inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch" and "The inactive patron report can be filtered by patron profile". These are one requirement: the inactive patron report can be filtered by home branch and patron profile.

    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "These recurring reports cover a broad set of maintenance needs across four sources, but each remains a specific management report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R048",
   "name": "Batch Status Conversion",
   "description": "The system must provide a report or workflow for converting many selected items from one status to another in one batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Batch status conversion saves staff effort when handling many selected records, but it is a specialized cleanup workflow."
  },
  {

   "description": "The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "A separate confirmation helps prevent unintended destructive purges, although deletion itself is a specialized workflow."
  },
  {
   "id": "R050",
   "name": "Deletion Audit Logging",
   "description": "The system must record completed and denied deletion attempts, including record type, record ID, timestamp, user, user branch, library system, and, where required, deletion reason; deletion data must support counts and queries by branch, system, date range, user, record type, and highest-volume users.",

    "D06",
    "D07",
    "D10",
    "D15",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Detailed deletion logs support accountability and investigation across several organizational dimensions, but deletion auditing is not the system's primary workflow."
  },
  {
   "id": "R051",
   "name": "Protected Purge Reports",
   "description": "Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Read-only candidate reports prevent an inspection step from altering records, providing a valuable safeguard for purge work."
  },
  {
   "id": "R052",
   "name": "Purge Audit Trail",
   "description": "The system must record who purged each record and when.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D06"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Recording who purged a record and when supports accountability, but this audit detail is requested by one source."
  },
  {
   "id": "R053",
   "name": "Purge Candidate Identification",
   "description": "The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.",

    "D06",
    "D10",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Customizable purge criteria help staff identify stale or unsuitable records consistently, though identification can be delivered after core reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R054",
   "name": "Activity Cross Tabulation",
   "description": "Activity reports must show checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, cross-tabulated by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Cross-tabulation supports analysis of activity across branches, hours, and patron groups, but is a specialized output of reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R055",
   "name": "Inactive Patron Reporting",
   "description": "The system must report patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, including OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access; the threshold must support any number of days, including 30, 90, 180, and 365.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D09",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Identifying inactive patrons across circulation and electronic activity supports outreach and account management, but is one specialized report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R056",
   "name": "Null Demographic Inclusion",
   "description": "Patron queries and reports must include patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank rather than silently excluding them.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Including blank demographics avoids silently skewing patron results, a concern raised in two sources."
  },
  {
   "id": "R057",
   "name": "Null Field Inclusion",
   "description": "Report results must include null and blank fields rather than excluding records or values containing them.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D08",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Including null and blank fields prevents records from disappearing from results, a data-completeness concern raised by five sources."
  },
  {
   "id": "R058",
   "name": "Inactive Patron Exceptions",
   "description": "The inactive patron report must separate patrons with outstanding fines and allow exclusion of do-not-disturb patrons, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Separating fines and excluding sensitive or opted-out groups helps staff use outreach results appropriately, though it extends one report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R059",
   "name": "Report Export Formats",
   "description": "Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09",
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D19",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV output lets staff use results in common tools, but the reports remain usable in the system without each format."
  },
  {
   "id": "R060",
   "name": "Scalable Inactive Reporting",
   "description": "For environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, inactive patron reports must run as background operations and cache slow activity-query results for reuse.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D09"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Background execution and caching help inactive reports remain usable at the stated patron scale, but are targeted optimizations for one report."
  },
  {
   "id": "R061",
   "name": "Acquisitions Cataloging Integration",
   "description": "Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Using the enterprise acquisitions and cataloging data avoids duplicating those functions, while those workflows remain outside this system's scope."
  },
  {
   "id": "R062",
   "name": "Anonymized Demographic Statistics",
   "description": "The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, a useful cross-source analysis capability."
  },
  {
   "id": "R063",
   "name": "Bibliographic Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide bibliographic reports for record counts, edited records, records added by user and branch, records without attached volumes or items, and records missing specified MARC fields.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Bibliographic reports help staff review records and identify missing data, but are one component of the wider management-reporting suite."
  },
  {
   "id": "R064",
   "name": "Bills Report Suite",
   "description": "The system must provide reports for current patron bills, detailed payments, forgive/work/goods payments, voids, and aged debt with detailed aging periods.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Bill and debt reports support financial follow-up, but are a specific part of the wider financial reporting capability."
  },
  {
   "id": "R065",
   "name": "Collection Value Reports",
   "description": "The system must report item values from purchase-price or other item-record data for the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D11",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Collection-value reporting supports budgeting and collection evaluation, though value analysis is one specialized management need."
  },
  {
   "id": "R066",

   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Migrating templates, permissions, and queries reduces configuration rework across environments, but the environments can function without automated migration."
  },
  {
   "id": "R067",
   "name": "Consortium Statistical Reports",
   "description": "The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D17"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Consortium-wide statistical reports let the global administrator evaluate network performance, but are a specific reporting scope."
  },
  {
   "id": "R068",
   "name": "Data Quality Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Data-quality reports help staff find records needing correction, and four sources request such operational oversight."

  {
   "id": "R069",
   "name": "Director Financial Reports",
   "description": "The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Director-level financial reports support leadership oversight, though they serve a specific audience and reporting domain."

  {
   "id": "R070",
   "name": "Environment Separation",
   "description": "The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D16",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks environment separation Medium Priority, and safe training and development spaces are useful without being prerequisites for live reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R071",
   "name": "Error Feedback",

   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks UD-4 Medium Priority, and detailed feedback helps administrators diagnose query problems but is not required for basic reporting."
  },
  {
   "id": "R072",

   "description": "The system must provide predefined reports for library boards and executive users, including Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid statistics and traffic and usage cross-tabulations by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Executive and board reports support oversight and required statistical submissions, but they are a distinct audience-specific report collection."

  {

    "D10",
    "D11"

    "D11"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Associating financial events with patron and item records enables useful reconciliation and joins, but is a specialized data capability."

    "D11",
    "D14"

   "priority_justification": "Shared templates give member branches a common starting point for management reports, but remain one way to meet reporting needs."

  {

   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Preselected on-demand reports support maintenance and collection development, though they are one delivery mode among several."

    "D19"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Querying OPAC-created holds and circulation makes patron-interface activity available to management reports without altering operational records."

  {

    "D10",
    "D20"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Renewal and return-speed statistics help assess patron behavior and material use, but are analytical additions to core reporting."

    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D20"

   "priority_justification": "Pivot-table output helps users summarize and explore results, and multiple sources request it as a useful analysis format."

   "id": "R082",

   "description": "The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.",
   "source_doc_ids": [
    "D10",
    "D18",
    "D19"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D10 marks process documentation Medium Priority, and it helps administrators understand imports, validation, and reporting without blocking system operation."

    "D14"

   "priority_justification": "Showing query selections and date criteria makes results easier to interpret and reproduce, though it does not produce the underlying report data."

  {

   "priority_justification": "Current-data reporting helps staff see recent activity, but some reporting needs can be met using scheduled or historical data."

    "D20"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Cancelling queued or running reports helps reclaim resources and correct mistaken submissions, with four sources requesting the control."

    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D20"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Fine-grained report permissions help administrators safely share data and tools, complementing the broader access-control capability."

    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D18",
    "D20"

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Queue visibility helps users understand delays and failures, and five sources request this useful operational transparency."

   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "D12 describes prioritization as crucial, and controlling queue order can help time-sensitive reports finish ahead of resource-heavy work."

  {
   "id": "R089",

    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Scheduling recurring reports reduces repeated staff work and is requested by three sources, but reports can also be run manually."

  {

    "D10",
    "D12",
    "D14",
    "D20"
   ],

    "D10",
    "D14",
    "D15",
    "D20"

    "D10",
    "D13",
    "D18"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Individual authentication preserves accountability for staff activity, while badge login is an optional convenience rather than a core reporting feature."
  },
  {

    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",

  {

    "D10",
    "D20"
   ],
   "priority": "Medium",
   "priority_justification": "Summaries by branch and patron grouping help managers compare checkouts and holds, but are a specific set of transaction views."

    "D15"

    "D19"

   "priority_justification": "Standard vendor-data exchange supports acquisitions and related management processes, but the reporting system can deliver value without automating every exchange."

  {

    "D10",
    "D20"

  {

    "D02"

  {

    "D02"
   ],
   "priority": "Low",
   "priority_justification": "CSV export is a useful convenience for further analysis, but the capacity data remains usable within the system without it."

  {

Recording deletion attempts and providing counts and queries over the resulting data are separate capabilities: one creates the audit record, while the other analyzes it.

Retaining detailed transactions, preserving indefinite aggregates, and grouping transactions for analysis are separate data-retention and reporting capabilities.

messages.content:
You resolve a group of related review issues in a requirements document. The user message is JSON with the issues (one or more, sharing requirements), the full text of every involved requirement (ids, sources, source_priority_note) and the glossary.

Resolve the group jointly and return ONE consistent result: replacements (which take the place of all involved requirements) and blacklist_entries (involved requirements discarded on purpose). Decide the fate of each involved requirement once, taking every issue into account; each ends up in a replacement or in the blacklist. Replacements cover only the content of the involved requirements: add nothing new, and never duplicate content across replacements.

Prefer rewording or narrowing to discarding. Blacklist only an item that is nonsensical, unsupported by its sources, or genuinely incompatible with a better-supported requirement. Each blacklist entry names the discarded requirement by its id and gives a one-paragraph reason that says which sources back each side.

By issue type:
- duplicate: one replacement that keeps every detail; nothing is blacklisted.
- conflict: keep or rewrite the better-supported side and blacklist the other; the reason says why the kept side wins (more sources, more recent, more authoritative).
- nonsense: blacklist the item; no replacement.
- wording: one rewritten replacement per involved requirement in glossary vocabulary, same meaning.
- priority: return the involved requirements unchanged (priority is reassigned later).
- too_broad: split into MORE SPECIFIC requirements, each naming a concrete capability from the original's content; never a more general or vaguer item, and never one that covers more than the original. Use the fewest pieces that satisfy the definition, usually two or three and at most 4 per requirement (if more seem needed, take the 4 largest coherent capabilities); never one per option or field. Together the pieces keep every detail.
- too_narrow: exactly one replacement for the pair: the parent with the detail folded in, as one coherent paragraph of plain prose that names the options, filters or fields in a sentence (never a semicolon-separated list of sub-capabilities). Nothing is blacklisted.

Sources: leave source_doc_ids empty and narrowing_reason null to inherit the union of the involved sources. Only when a replacement (for example one split piece) is supported by a subset, list that subset and explain why in narrowing_reason.

source_priority_note travels only with the content it belongs to: a merged replacement gets the notes of the items merged into it; each split piece gets only the notes that apply to its content (null when none clearly does).

Text: Each requirement has a short descriptive name (3 to 8 words) and a one-paragraph description that keeps the concrete facts (numbers, fields, roles). Use glossary terms and no provenance or priority prose. Never write a pointer requirement: a requirement states the capability itself, never "the reports listed in the specification/appendix", "see section X" or "the examples identified in ...". When a source contains a catalogue or list of items (for example an appendix of report types), each item becomes its own requirement or is explicitly folded into a named requirement whose description covers it. In names, descriptions and reasons, refer to other requirements by name, never by id: ids are renumbered later.

Definition of a requirement: A requirement describes one capability, rule or quality the system must provide, at the level a tester would write one acceptance test for. It names what, for whom, and under what condition, and it is independent of how it is implemented. Two statements are the same requirement if a tester would write one test for both. A statement is too broad if its acceptance test would have to be several unrelated tests. A statement is too narrow if it only makes sense as a detail of another requirement, such as one filter option of a report.

issues.explanation: R045 is the detail: restricting transfer permissions to specified roles is already covered by R007's requirement for role-appropriate transfer permissions.

replacements.name: Role-Based Transfer Access
replacements.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, with changes to role assignments changing permissions. The library automation system must support Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role and transfers restricted to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.
replacements.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

issues.explanation: R046 is the detail: it specifies an overdue subset of the transit-to and transit-from reporting already required by R010.

replacements.name: Transit Report Suite
replacements.description: The system must provide reports for items in transit to a destination branch and items in transit by sending branch, including one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.
replacements.source_priority_note: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination

issues.explanation: R056 is the detail: including null or blank patron demographic fields is a specific case of R057's general null-and-blank inclusion rule for report results.

replacements.name: Null and Blank Field Inclusion
replacements.description: Patron queries and reports must include records and values with null or blank fields, including patrons whose optional demographic fields are null or blank, rather than silently excluding them.

issues.explanation: R058 is the detail: its exceptions and fine separation refine the inactive-patron report required by R055.
R111 is the detail: address inclusion and CSV export are additional output details of the inactive-patron report required by R055.
R112 is the detail: grouping inactive patrons by organizational scope refines the report required by R055.

replacements.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
replacements.description: The system must provide an inactive patron report for patrons with no circulation and no electronic activity during a configurable preceding period, where the threshold supports any number of days including 30, 90, 180, and 365 and electronic activity includes OPAC or patron-account logins, online holds, online renewals, and integrated digital-resource access. The report must separate patrons with outstanding fines, allow exclusion of patrons marked do-not-disturb, VIP patrons, staff members, and patrons who opted out of communications, include each patron's current mailing address, support CSV export for upload to an outreach system, and list or group results by configurable organizational scopes including the library system, home branch, and county so users can see system totals and assign work to branches.

issues.explanation: R060's background execution for a long-running report is a specific case of R015's background processing requirement. Its caching clause is an additional optimization, but does not make the background-processing part a separate report capability.

replacements.name: Background Report Processing
replacements.description: Long-running reports, including inactive patron reports in environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, must execute as background operations or through a queue without occupying the user interface, and the system must cache slow activity-query results for reuse.

issues.explanation: R069 is the detail: it specifies an audience for financial reports, while R075 already requires financial reporting across balances, fines, waivers, and payments.

replacements.name: Director-Level Financial Reports
replacements.description: The system must provide financial reports suitable for library directors and other users requiring director-level financial information, including patron balances by patron, home branch, and library system, fines and charges by period and charge type, waived fines by period and branch, and payments by period, collecting branch, payment channel, and payment type.

issues.explanation: R077 is the detail: templates for consortium member branches are already within R030's requirement for predefined reports and templates covering branches' management needs.

replacements.name: Branch Management Reports and Templates
replacements.description: The system must provide predefined reports and report templates needed to cover the management reporting needs of all consortium member branches.

issues.explanation: R078 is the detail: it specifies maintenance and collection-development uses for on-demand reports, a report type already required by R031.

replacements.name: Report Types and Uses
replacements.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports, noncanned on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for maintenance and collection-development activities, and open-template reports with selectable attributes for circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records.

issues.explanation: R102 is the detail: side-by-side branch comparison refines the shelf-space analysis already required by R037.

replacements.name: Shelf Space Analysis
replacements.description: The system must provide shelf-space analysis that compares, side by side, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space so users can identify differences and outliers, with views by branch and for the library system, selectable date ranges such as Q1 or Q2, collection percentages based on item counts, circulation percentages based on checkouts, and shelf-space estimates based on item dimensions or item count when dimensions are unavailable.

issues.explanation: R106 is the detail: printable pull lists refine the pull-list option already included in R038's transfer capability.

replacements.name: Batch Item Transfers
replacements.description: Authorized staff must be able to transfer selected batches of items between branches and other destinations, including mobile libraries, outreach programs, warehouses, book sales, and event locations, by changing item locations or generating printable pull lists identifying items selected for transfer; the operation must process approximately 9.6 million items without excessive database locking.

issues.explanation: R119 is the detail: classifying hold counts by placement method is a specific breakdown of the hold-activity reporting and cross-tabulation required by R054.

replacements.name: Activity Cross-Tabulation
replacements.description: Activity reports must show counts of checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, cross-tabulated by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location, and must classify hold-request counts by placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

issues.explanation: R123 is the detail: integrated help for the reporting interface is a specific instance of the searchable, in-system help required by R022.

replacements.name: Integrated Accessible System Help
replacements.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions, is accessible within the system and to screen readers, and includes integrated online help for the reporting interface.
replacements.source_priority_note: D10 marks UD-3 High Priority

issues.explanation: R127 is the detail: historical bill reporting is explicitly included in R001's historical reporting requirement.

replacements.name: Historical Reporting
replacements.description: The system must provide historical reports through preserved data or a reporting warehouse, retrieving values as they existed at a specified date or date range, including past bills and shelving locations.

issues.explanation: The name says “Vendor And Library Integration,” but the description specifies only a centralized reporting service across branches and says nothing about vendor integration.

replacements.name: Centralized Branch Reporting Service
replacements.description: The system must provide a centralized service that accepts input from and serves multiple branches as a single reporting source of truth.

issues.explanation: The requirement allows a “report” as an alternative to a workflow for converting item statuses. A report alone cannot perform the required conversion, so the description does not unambiguously require the conversion capability.

replacements.name: Batch Status Conversion
replacements.description: The system must provide a workflow that converts many selected items from one status to another in a single batch, such as changing 100 missing items to discard/weed.

messages.content:
You assign priorities to software requirements. The user message is JSON with "fixed" requirements whose priority is already decided (for calibration only, do not output them) and numbered "items" that need a priority.

Priority scale:
- High: Core to the system's purpose or requested by many stakeholders; the system is not acceptable without it.
- Medium: Clearly valuable and requested, but the system can go live without it and add it in a later release.
- Low: Nice to have, requested by a single stakeholder or marginal to the core workflows; implement only if time allows.

Hard rule, applied first: if an item's source_priority_note reports an explicit priority marker in a specification document (for example [*] or High in a draft SRS), a source calling the item critical, or wording that it is legally required, mandatory, non-negotiable or a compliance obligation, the priority is High and the justification names that source. An individual's emphasis in an e-mail or interview ("crucial", "essential", "we really need") is evidence for the judgment below, not a trigger.

Judge every other item by how central it is to the system's purpose, how many source documents ask for it (source_doc_ids) and whether the system can work without it, calibrated against the fixed requirements:
- Medium is not a default: clear value without urgency is Medium; nice-to-have and single-stakeholder conveniences are Low. Aim for a defensible spread across the three levels.
- A feature mentioned once in passing by one person is not High on its own, nor is a requirement that only exists as a thin list heading (for example "provide canned reports").
- A sub-feature of a report or utility is never higher than the report or utility.

Return exactly one entry per numbered item, with no missing or duplicate indices. justification is one sentence that agrees with the level: a justification that calls the item essential, critical, fundamental or mandatory belongs to a High item, Medium justifications describe clear value without urgency, Low ones a nice-to-have. It is not circular: instead of "X is essential", say who depends on it, what fails without it, or which signal in the sources decided it.

items.justification: Seven source documents call for collection and material-use analysis, and managers depend on it to plan, evaluate, and oversee collections.
Branch capacity and demographic analysis helps managers assess local needs, although the reporting system can serve its core purpose without this specific analysis.
Staff-workflow and financial reporting helps administrators monitor operations and transactions, but it is one valuable reporting area among several.
Cross-branch performance analysis is repeatedly requested across seven documents and supports oversight of the consortium as a whole.
Item change and inventory reports help staff track collection activity and investigate record changes, but they are not the only way to meet management reporting needs.
Missing-item reporting is required by the fixed requirements, and the broader status reports also help staff manage overdue and in-transit materials.
D06 and D15 explicitly mark last-copy reporting critical, and these reports help catalogers avoid inappropriate deletion while supporting collection decisions.
Batch status conversion can reduce repetitive item-maintenance work, though staff can still manage statuses without bulk conversion.
Check-in method counts help managers compare service channels and workload, but are a specialized part of circulation analysis.
Checkout and renewal counts directly support the fixed requirement for item-use reporting and help managers understand how materials are used.
Overdue and circulation-type reports help staff monitor circulation patterns, but they are a subset of the wider reporting scope.
Reports using patron and item attributes enable useful segmented circulation analysis, though the system can operate without every listed dimension.
Patron counts by demographic and location help branches understand who they serve, but they are one analytical capability within the broader reporting system.
Addition, expiration, and status reports help staff manage patron accounts, although these administrative reports are not required for every management workflow.
Survey answers and notes may inform selected patron analyses, but this specialized and potentially sensitive information is not needed for most reporting workflows.
Password-date reporting may help administrators monitor staff accounts, but it is a narrow administrative convenience rather than a central management-reporting need.
A cross-record query designer lets staff build reports across the system's principal data areas, and without it many requested analyses would require custom work.
Administrative controls over query fields and tools help manage access and usability, but the query designer remains useful without extensive configuration.
Hold and transit reports help staff coordinate material movement and resolve delays, though they serve a specialized operational workflow.
Reports on inactive, last-copy, and missing items support collection management, but this periodic report suite is narrower than the overall reporting purpose.
Catalog and item integrity reports help staff find data problems that can impede operations, but they are a maintenance capability rather than a core reporting outcome.
A report on patrons with invalid home branches helps correct a specific data issue, but this narrow check is not central to system use.
Recording completed and denied deletions gives administrators a useful accountability trail, although the reporting system can function without deletion auditing.
Analyzing deletion records can help identify patterns after an audit trail exists, but it is a secondary capability built on the audit function.
Predefined board and executive reports save leadership time, but those users can still obtain oversight information through other reports.
A Georgia Annual Report supports state reporting needs, though it is a specific report rather than a general system capability.
State Aid statistics help users prepare a specific reporting submission, but this report can be added separately from core management analytics.
Traffic cross-tabulations provide useful comparisons across locations and user groups, but they are one specialized form of analysis.
Configurable detailed transaction retention supports historical analysis and retention planning, but its value depends on the reporting period each use case requires.
The fixed privacy-preserving archive requirement calls for indefinite monthly and annual aggregates where required, and this item provides that preservation.
Grouping transactions across operational dimensions supports useful trend analysis, but the system can provide other management reports without every grouping.
Tracking uncataloged materials makes their use visible before catalog records exist, which helps libraries manage these materials but serves a narrower workflow.
Rapid distribution with minimal branch labor would improve handling of uncataloged materials, but it is a workflow convenience rather than a reporting-system foundation.
Identifying use of uncataloged materials helps managers assess whether those materials are serving patrons, though it covers a limited collection segment.
Including uncataloged transactions prevents circulation summaries from omitting this material use, but the requirement applies to a narrower set of materials.
Material-volume reporting helps managers track collection size and recent acquisitions by branch or system, but it is a focused management report.
Branch capacity comparisons and trends help managers allocate space and monitor growth across the consortium, but the system can provide other oversight reports without them.
D10 marks CO-4 High Priority, and D16 identifies role-based access control as essential; without it, staff cannot be reliably limited to authorized reporting and transfer actions.
D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination, and delayed or untracked transfers can disrupt service across branches.
Including null and blank values helps prevent incomplete demographic data from silently skewing patron reports, though it is an accuracy safeguard within those reports.
The inactive-patron report can support targeted outreach and workload assignment, but this specialized workflow is not necessary for other management reporting.
The fixed open-hours performance requirement calls for reports not to disrupt other services, and background processing helps meet that need for large, slow queries.
Director-level financial summaries help leadership monitor balances, charges, waivers, and payments, but they are a defined subset of financial reporting.
Multiple source documents request management reports for consortium branches, and without suitable reports and templates branch managers would lack a consistent way to meet routine oversight needs.
Canned, on-demand, and open-template reports give users practical ways to cover routine and changing needs across core record types, making the system usable for its reporting purpose.
Shelf-space analysis helps managers compare collection allocation with use and identify outliers, but it is a specialized planning tool.
Batch transfers reduce effort when moving large groups of items, but staff can still perform transfers through other processes if this workflow is deferred.
Cross-tabulated activity counts help managers compare service channels, locations, and patron groups, but they are one form of operational analysis.
D10 marks UD-3 High Priority, and accessible, searchable help lets staff learn and use reporting functions without relying solely on direct support.
Historical reporting helps users understand what values and locations were at a past date, but it requires preserved data beyond the system's basic current-state reports.
A centralized reporting service can give branches a consistent source of information, but the system can provide useful reports without this particular service architecture.
Batch status conversion saves staff time when many items need the same change, though individual updates remain possible if the batch workflow is deferred.

inputs.name: Consortium Scale
inputs.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-1 High Priority, and consortium-scale support is necessary for the system to serve its stated 286-branch environment.

inputs.name: Item Use Metrics
inputs.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and counts by fiscal-year, month, or other usage date range, including checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged circulation breakdowns.
inputs.priority_justification: Six sources request item-use counts across time periods and usage types, making circulation and collection-use measurement a central reporting need.

inputs.name: Missing Damaged Reports
inputs.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.
inputs.priority_justification: D05 calls the per-branch report crucial for accountability, and four additional sources request missing or damaged item reporting.
inputs.source_priority_note: D05 calls the per-branch missing/damaged report crucial for accountability

inputs.name: Patron Report Filtering
inputs.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.
inputs.priority_justification: D08 calls these reports essential, and demographic and circulation filtering is a central way staff answer patron-service and planning questions.

inputs.name: Accounting Data Retention
inputs.description: The system must archive financial data according to state and local requirements and enforce applicable retention policies, including seven years of audit data where required.
inputs.priority_justification: Applicable financial retention rules, including required audit-data periods, must be enforced to support accountable records management.

inputs.name: Assistive Technology Access
inputs.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
inputs.priority_justification: D16 and D18 identify Section 508 accessibility as a legal requirement and mandatory, making assistive-technology access a compliance obligation.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

inputs.name: Client And Browser Access
inputs.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority and D18 calls browser/client access critical, so staff access to the system depends on this capability.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical

inputs.name: Financial Compliance
inputs.description: Financial reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
inputs.priority_justification: Financial reports and archiving must meet the specified public-sector accounting and audit requirements for the system to serve its users.

inputs.name: Management Reporting Scope
inputs.description: The reporting functionality must support management planning, evaluation, and oversight rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled by the OPAC and circulation client.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources define management planning, evaluation, and oversight as the reporting system's scope, distinguishing it from patron-facing operations.

inputs.name: OPAC Preservation
inputs.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority, and management reporting that degrades patron access would compromise the underlying library service.
inputs.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

inputs.name: Open-Hours Performance
inputs.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.
inputs.priority_justification: Five sources request safe operation during open or peak hours, and contention that disrupts circulation or OPAC access would impair the system's core use.

inputs.name: Payment Audit Ledger
inputs.description: The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.
inputs.priority_justification: D11 marks the payment ledger CRITICAL, and tracing applied payments is needed to reconcile patron financial records.

inputs.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
inputs.description: The system must retain transaction data for the legally required period while removing personally identifying patron information, preserving useful demographic statistics, and retaining monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely where required.
inputs.priority_justification: D12 identifies state-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements, requiring archival statistics without retained identifying data.
inputs.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

inputs.name: Record Data Specifications
inputs.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-1 High Priority, and accurate data specifications support the cross-record reporting the product must deliver.

inputs.name: Relational Database Support
inputs.description: The system must use and operate with a fully relational database, support complex joins, and not require a denormalized reporting schema that can cause synchronization problems.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-1 High Priority, and the requested relational access underpins the system's complex cross-record reporting.

inputs.name: Report Accuracy
inputs.description: Report output must be tested and demonstrated to be accurate and dependable.
inputs.priority_justification: Inaccurate or unreliable reports undermine the system's central purpose of supporting management decisions.

inputs.name: Server Platform Support
inputs.description: The system must operate on Linux and Solaris servers, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware where specified.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-2 High Priority, specifying the server platforms the product must support in the target environment.

inputs.name: Standards Compliant HTML
inputs.description: Web interfaces, reports, and online help must produce HTML that validates against applicable web standards.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-2 High Priority, establishing standards-compliant HTML as a specified product constraint.

inputs.name: Select Query Results Manually
inputs.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative actions.
inputs.priority_justification: Manual result selection gives staff control over records chosen for administrative actions, complementing the transfer workflow.

inputs.name: Transfer Candidate Queries
inputs.description: Staff must be able to query for candidate items for transfer using criteria such as genre, collection area, and circulation inactivity, including items that have not circulated for six months.
inputs.priority_justification: Transfer-candidate queries help staff identify suitable items using several sources' requested criteria, while transfers can still be initiated through other selection methods.

inputs.name: Transfer Confirmation Preview
inputs.description: Before execution, the system must show a transfer preview containing the item count and source and destination locations and require staff confirmation.
inputs.priority_justification: A preview and confirmation reduce accidental transfers by showing the affected count and locations before execution.

inputs.name: Transfer Item Selection
inputs.description: Staff must be able to manually select individual titles or items from transfer-query results before executing a transfer, such as selecting 25 items from 100 candidates.
inputs.priority_justification: Manual selection lets staff limit transfers to appropriate results and avoid moving every candidate, improving control of the transfer workflow.

inputs.name: Transfer Location Updates
inputs.description: The system must update the location field and associated item records for selected items moved to a new location.
inputs.priority_justification: Updating item locations is needed to keep records accurate when a transfer occurs, although it supports a secondary operational workflow.

inputs.name: Transfer Reversion
inputs.description: The system must return transferred items to their original locations after a configured period or configured event, including a status change to sold or returned or checkout at the destination.
inputs.priority_justification: Configured reversion helps return items after temporary placements or specified events, but transfers can function without automated returns.

inputs.name: Confirmed Purge Deletion
inputs.description: The system must require a separate confirmation before executing purge deletions.
inputs.priority_justification: A separate confirmation helps prevent unintended destructive purges, although deletion itself is a specialized workflow.

inputs.name: Protected Purge Reports
inputs.description: Reports identifying purge candidates must be read-only and must not delete or modify candidate records.
inputs.priority_justification: Read-only candidate reports prevent an inspection step from altering records, providing a valuable safeguard for purge work.

inputs.name: Purge Candidate Identification
inputs.description: The system must identify item records eligible for purging using customizable status, duration, and circulation criteria, including missing, discard/weed, or damaged status, time in status, and no circulation for a specified period; criteria must support Boolean combinations such as missing for six months and no circulation for two years.
inputs.priority_justification: Customizable purge criteria help staff identify stale or unsuitable records consistently, though identification can be delivered after core reporting.

inputs.name: Report Export Formats
inputs.description: Report output must be available in Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.
inputs.priority_justification: Excel-compatible, HTML, and CSV output lets staff use results in common tools, but the reports remain usable in the system without each format.

inputs.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
inputs.description: Management processes must read and use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise Library Automation System, including Acquisitions and Cataloging, without managing those functions.
inputs.priority_justification: Using the enterprise acquisitions and cataloging data avoids duplicating those functions, while those workflows remain outside this system's scope.

inputs.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
inputs.description: The system must provide anonymized transaction and patron statistics by geographic region, ZIP code, age range, and other useful demographic attributes without disclosing personally identifiable information.
inputs.priority_justification: Anonymized demographic statistics support planning while protecting patron identity, a useful cross-source analysis capability.

inputs.name: Bibliographic Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide bibliographic reports for record counts, edited records, records added by user and branch, records without attached volumes or items, and records missing specified MARC fields.
inputs.priority_justification: Bibliographic reports help staff review records and identify missing data, but are one component of the wider management-reporting suite.

inputs.name: Bills Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide reports for current patron bills, detailed payments, forgive/work/goods payments, voids, and aged debt with detailed aging periods.
inputs.priority_justification: Bill and debt reports support financial follow-up, but are a specific part of the wider financial reporting capability.

inputs.name: Configuration Migration
inputs.description: The system must export and import report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration between development, training, and production environments.
inputs.priority_justification: Migrating templates, permissions, and queries reduces configuration rework across environments, but the environments can function without automated migration.

inputs.name: Consortium Statistical Reports
inputs.description: The Global System Administrator must be able to generate statistical reports for the entire library consortium.
inputs.priority_justification: Consortium-wide statistical reports let the global administrator evaluate network performance, but are a specific reporting scope.

inputs.name: Data Quality Reports
inputs.description: The system must provide data-quality reports identifying invalid item types, excessively long call numbers, bibliographic records without items, and other data problems.
inputs.priority_justification: Data-quality reports help staff find records needing correction, and four sources request such operational oversight.

inputs.name: Environment Separation
inputs.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments, including a training environment safe for experimentation without affecting production.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks environment separation Medium Priority, and safe training and development spaces are useful without being prerequisites for live reporting.

inputs.name: Error Feedback
inputs.description: The system must provide high-level error reporting and low-level query-specific feedback to administrators, including relevant table, field, and error type when available.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-4 Medium Priority, and detailed feedback helps administrators diagnose query problems but is not required for basic reporting.

inputs.name: Financial Data Updates
inputs.description: Authorized staff must be able to update financial information easily, and a payment made at a staff desk must be reflected immediately.
inputs.priority_justification: Immediate reflection of desk payments keeps financial information current, though financial updates are a secondary system workflow.

inputs.name: Financial Record Association
inputs.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waivers, payments, and ecommerce transactions with relevant patron and item records and support joins between patron and item financial data.
inputs.priority_justification: Associating financial events with patron and item records enables useful reconciliation and joins, but is a specialized data capability.

inputs.name: Hold Report Suite
inputs.description: The system must provide hold reports for purchase alerts, items sent or received for holds, IntraPINES loans, unfilled holds, annual totals, and stale holds remaining beyond the permitted pickup period.
inputs.priority_justification: Hold reports help branches monitor requests and identify stale or unfilled holds, but are a defined circulation subdomain.

inputs.name: OPAC Data Querying
inputs.description: Management processes must query patron-interface data created in the OPAC, including holds and circulation, without modifying that data.
inputs.priority_justification: Querying OPAC-created holds and circulation makes patron-interface activity available to management reports without altering operational records.

inputs.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
inputs.description: The system must produce statistics about patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal likelihood, renewal rates, and the percentage of branch checkouts that are renewals.
inputs.priority_justification: Renewal and return-speed statistics help assess patron behavior and material use, but are analytical additions to core reporting.

inputs.name: Pivot Table Output
inputs.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.
inputs.priority_justification: Pivot-table output helps users summarize and explore results, and multiple sources request it as a useful analysis format.

inputs.name: Process Documentation
inputs.description: The product must document major processes, including bibliographic import and export, validation against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.
inputs.priority_justification: D10 marks process documentation Medium Priority, and it helps administrators understand imports, validation, and reporting without blocking system operation.

inputs.name: Query Criteria Display
inputs.description: Report results must display the query selections, report name, and selected date criteria used to produce them.
inputs.priority_justification: Showing query selections and date criteria makes results easier to interpret and reproduce, though it does not produce the underlying report data.

inputs.name: Real Time Reporting
inputs.description: The system must support reports using current data in real time, including activity during busy periods.
inputs.priority_justification: Current-data reporting helps staff see recent activity, but some reporting needs can be met using scheduled or historical data.

inputs.name: Report Cancellation
inputs.description: Users must be able to cancel scheduled, queued, or currently running reports, including during processing.
inputs.priority_justification: Cancelling queued or running reports helps reclaim resources and correct mistaken submissions, with four sources requesting the control.

inputs.name: Report Permission Administration
inputs.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions for creating, cloning, running, and accessing reports, filters, data sets, and shared folders, including administrator-controlled shared folders that allow or prohibit specific report access.
inputs.priority_justification: Fine-grained report permissions help administrators safely share data and tools, complementing the broader access-control capability.

inputs.name: Report Queue Monitoring
inputs.description: Users must be able to see report queue contents, position, number of reports ahead, submission time, and status such as waiting, running, completed, or failed.
inputs.priority_justification: Queue visibility helps users understand delays and failures, and five sources request this useful operational transparency.

inputs.name: Report Queue Prioritization
inputs.description: Authorized users or processes must be able to prioritize selected report types so important reports execute ahead of lower-priority or resource-consuming reports.
inputs.priority_justification: D12 describes prioritization as crucial, and controlling queue order can help time-sensitive reports finish ahead of resource-heavy work.
inputs.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial

inputs.name: Report Scheduling
inputs.description: Users must be able to run reports as soon as possible or schedule them hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, including recurring reports that can be edited by changing selections or email addresses.
inputs.priority_justification: Scheduling recurring reports reduces repeated staff work and is requested by three sources, but reports can also be run manually.

inputs.name: Report Template Controls
inputs.description: Authorized administrators must create shared report templates that staff can run as-is or modify within controlled limits on filters and display fields, without compromising intended results or exposing deleted items; authorized users must be able to clone templates and edit permitted display options.
inputs.priority_justification: Shared templates let administrators standardize reports while giving staff controlled flexibility, a useful capability requested by four sources.

inputs.name: Save Reusable Queries
inputs.description: The system must allow staff to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting activities.
inputs.priority_justification: Reusable queries reduce repeated setup effort across several reporting activities, but reports can still be produced without saving them.

inputs.name: Staff Authentication
inputs.description: The system must support optional employee-card or badge login and individual username-and-password login as a fallback; every login must identify the individual staff member and card login must not bypass individual authentication.
inputs.priority_justification: Individual authentication preserves accountability for staff activity, while badge login is an optional convenience rather than a core reporting feature.

inputs.name: Transaction Summary Reports
inputs.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and checkouts by patron, branch, selected branch groups, library system, and county, including checkout and hold subtotals and hold states such as active, frozen, and frozen-until.
inputs.priority_justification: Summaries by branch and patron grouping help managers compare checkouts and holds, but are a specific set of transaction views.

inputs.name: Vendor Data Integration
